text: What is so special about green tea? The Chinese and Indians {{16}} it for at least 4,000 years to treat everything from headache to depression. Researchers at Purdue University recently concluded that a compound in green tea {{17}} the growth of cancer cells. Green tea is also helpful {{18}} infection and damaged immune function. The secret power of green tea is its richness in a powerful anti-oxidant.

Green tea and black tea come from the same plant. Their {{19}} is in the processing. Green tea is dried but not fermented, and this shorter processing gives it a lighter flavor than black tea. It also helps retain the tea’s beneficial chemicals. That is {{20}} green tea is so good for health. The only reported negative effect of drinking green tea is a possible allergic reaction and insomnia due to the caffeine it contains.

qs.ex: 後面有 for at least 4,000 years，表示從過去持續到現在的動作，應用現在完成式或現在完成進行式，選項中只有 (D) have been using 符合。
依文意，綠茶中的化合物應是抑制癌細胞的生長，slow down 意為「減緩」，故選 (B) slows down。
be helpful for 意為「對……有幫助」，後接 infection 等病症，故選 (A) for。
前句說綠茶與紅茶來自同一種植物，後句說差別在加工過程，所以空格填 difference（差異），故選 (C)。
That is why + 結果，表示「這就是……的原因」，前句已說明原因，故選 (D) why。

zh: 綠茶究竟有什麼特別之處？中國人和印度人至少已經飲用綠茶四千年，用來治療從頭痛到憂鬱症的各種病症。普渡大學的研究人員最近斷定，綠茶中的一種化合物會減緩癌細胞的生長。綠茶也有助於對抗感染、改善受損的免疫功能。綠茶的神祕力量在於它富含一種強力的抗氧化物。
綠茶和紅茶來自同一種植物，兩者的差異在於加工方式。綠茶經過乾燥但不發酵，這種較短的加工過程使它的味道比紅茶清淡，也有助於保留茶中對人體有益的化學物質。這就是綠茶對健康如此有益的原因。據報導，飲用綠茶唯一的負面影響，是可能引起過敏反應，以及其所含咖啡因導致的失眠。
title: 綠茶的功效

text: A wise woman traveling in the mountains found a precious stone. The next day she met another traveler who was hungry. The wise woman generously opened her bag to {{21}} her food with the traveler. When the hungry traveler saw the precious stone, he asked her to give it to him. The woman did {{22}} without hesitation. The traveler left, rejoicing. If he sold the stone, he thought, he {{23}} enough money for the rest of his life.

But in a few days he came back to find the woman. When he found her, he said, “I know how valuable this stone is, but I’m giving it back to you, {{24}} that you can give me something even more precious. You gave me the stone without asking for anything {{25}}. Please teach me what you have in your heart that makes you so generous.”

qs.ex: share A with B 意為「與 B 分享 A」，空格後有 her food with the traveler，故選 (C) share。
do so 代替前面的動詞片語 give it to him，表示「照做」，故選 (A) so。
he thought 引出旅人心裡的盤算：如果把寶石賣掉，就有足夠的錢過完下半輩子。這是對未來情況的假設，在過去式的敘述中，if 子句用過去式 sold，主要子句用 would + 原形動詞，故選 (C) would have；(D) would have had 用於與過去事實相反的假設，不合。
前面主要子句為完整句子，空格後 that 子句為受詞，用現在分詞表示附帶說明「希望……」，故選 (B) hoping。
in return 意為「作為回報」，女子給寶石而不求任何回報，故選 (D) in return。

zh: 一位智慧的女子在山中旅行時撿到一顆珍貴的寶石。隔天她遇到另一位飢餓的旅人，便慷慨地打開袋子，與這位旅人分享她的食物。這位飢餓的旅人看見那顆寶石後，請她把寶石給他。女子毫不猶豫地照做了。旅人欣喜地離開。他心想，如果把這顆寶石賣掉，他這輩子就會有足夠的錢可用。
但過了幾天，他回來找那位女子。找到她之後，他說：「我知道這顆寶石多麼珍貴，但我要把它還給你，希望你能給我某樣更珍貴的東西。你給了我寶石，卻不求任何回報。請教我，你心中究竟有什麼，讓你如此慷慨。」
title: 智者與寶石

text: Prague, the capital of the Czech Republic, is a very beautiful city. Situated on both banks of the winding River Vltava, Prague is like one big open-air museum. {{26}} some six hundred years of architecture nearly untouched by natural disaster or war, the city retains much of its medieval appearance. {{27}} you go, there are buildings in Romanic, Baroque, and Rococo styles that were popular hundreds of years ago. All of them successfully {{28}} the destruction of postwar redevelopment and remained unchanged. While the Iron Curtain was still in place under the communist government, Prague was {{29}} visited by foreigners. Since the 1990s, {{30}}, all that has changed. Prague is now one of the most popular tourist attractions in Europe.

qs.ex: With + 受詞 + 過去分詞片語（untouched…）表示附帶狀況或原因，「擁有……的建築」，故選 (B) With。
空格後為 you go, there are…，Wherever you go 意為「不論你去哪裡」，引導讓步副詞子句，故選 (D) Wherever。
escape the destruction 意為「逃過破壞」，才會 remained unchanged，故選 (A) escaped。
鐵幕時期與 1990 年代後「all that has changed」形成對比，當時遊客稀少，故選 (B) seldom（很少）。
前句說過去很少人造訪，後句說現在變成熱門景點，語意轉折，故選 (C) however。

zh: 捷克共和國的首都布拉格是一座非常美麗的城市。布拉格座落於蜿蜒的伏爾塔瓦河兩岸，就像一座巨大的露天博物館。由於擁有約六百年幾乎未受天災或戰爭破壞的建築，這座城市保留了許多中世紀的風貌。不論你走到哪裡，都有數百年前流行的羅馬式、巴洛克式與洛可可式建築。這些建築全都成功躲過了戰後重建的破壞，並維持原貌。在共產政權之下鐵幕仍然存在的時期，外國人很少造訪布拉格。然而，自一九九○年代以來，這一切都改變了。布拉格現在是歐洲最受歡迎的觀光勝地之一。
title: 布拉格古城

text: One day, a guru foresaw in a vision what he would be in his next life. Then he called his favorite disciple and asked him, “What would you do to thank me for all you have received from me?” The disciple said he would do whatever his guru asked him to do. Having received this {{31}}, the guru said, “Then this is what I’d like you to do for me. I’ve just {{32}} that I’ll die very soon and I’m going to be reborn as a pig. Do you see that sow eating garbage there in the yard? I’m going to be the fourth piglet of its next litter. You’ll {{33}} me by a mark on my brow. After that sow gives birth, find the fourth piglet with a mark on its brow and, with one {{34}} of your knife, slaughter it. I’ll then be {{35}} from a pig’s life. Will you do this for me?”

The disciple felt sad to hear this, but he agreed to do as he was told. Soon after their {{36}}, the guru died and the sow did have a litter of four little pigs. Then the disciple {{37}} his knife and picked out the little pig with a mark on its brow. When he was about to cut its throat, the little pig suddenly {{38}}, “Stop!” Before the disciple could recover from the {{39}} of hearing the little pig speak in a human voice, it continued, “Don’t kill me. I want to live on as a pig. When I asked you to kill me, I didn’t know what a pig’s life would be {{40}}. It’s great! Just let me go.”

qs.ex: Having received this ___ 缺名詞作受詞；弟子說願意做任何事，等於給了師父一個承諾，故選 (D) promise（名詞）。
I've just ___ that… 缺過去分詞（現在完成式），learn 意為「得知」，師父剛在異象中得知自己將死，故選 (G) learned（過去分詞）。
助動詞 will 後需原形動詞，recognize me by a mark 意為「憑記號認出我」，故選 (H) recognize（原形動詞）。
one ___ of your knife 需名詞，a stroke of a knife 指「一刀」，故選 (I) stroke（名詞）。
will be 後接形容詞或過去分詞，be released from 意為「從……解脫」，故選 (E) released（過去分詞）。
their ___ 需名詞，指師徒之間剛才的談話，故選 (B) conversation（名詞）。
空格前為主詞 the disciple，後為受詞 his knife，需過去式動詞，與 picked out 並列，磨利刀子準備宰殺，故選 (J) sharpened（動詞）。
suddenly 後接動詞，引號中的 “Stop!” 是喊叫的內容，故選 (F) screamed（過去式動詞）。
the ___ of hearing… 需名詞，聽見小豬說人話令人「震驚」，故選 (A) shock（名詞）。
what a pig's life would be like 意為「豬的生活是什麼樣子」，like 為介系詞，故選 (C) like。

zh: 有一天，一位大師在異象中預見了自己來世會變成什麼。於是他把最心愛的弟子叫來，問他：「你從我這裡得到了這麼多，你要怎麼感謝我？」弟子說，不論師父要他做什麼，他都願意去做。得到這個承諾後，大師說：「那麼，這就是我希望你為我做的事。我剛得知我很快就會死，並將轉世成一頭豬。你看到院子裡那頭正在吃垃圾的母豬嗎？我將成為牠下一胎的第四隻小豬。你要憑我眉間的一個記號認出我。等那頭母豬生產之後，找出眉間有記號的第四隻小豬，用你的刀一刀把牠宰了。這樣我就能從豬的一生中解脫。你願意為我做這件事嗎？」
弟子聽了很難過，但還是答應照吩咐去做。那次談話後不久，大師就過世了，母豬果然生下一窩四隻小豬。於是弟子磨利了刀子，挑出眉間有記號的那隻小豬。就在他準備割斷牠的喉嚨時，小豬突然尖叫：「住手！」弟子還來不及從聽見小豬用人聲說話的震驚中回過神來，小豬就繼續說：「別殺我。我想繼續當一頭豬。我要你殺我的時候，並不知道豬的生活是什麼樣子。真是太棒了！放我走吧。」
title: 師父的轉世請求

text: Art Fry was a researcher in the 3M Company. He was bothered by a small irritation every Sunday as he sang in the church choir. That is, after he {{16}} his pages in the hymn book with small bits of paper, the small pieces would invariably fall out all over the floor. One day, an idea {{17}} Art Fry. He remembered a kind of glue developed by a colleague that everyone thought {{18}} a failure because it did not stick very well. He then coated the glue on a paper sample and found that it was not only a good bookmark, but it was great for writing notes. It would stay in place {{19}} you wanted it to. Then you could remove it {{20}} damage. The resulting product was called the Post-it, one of 3M’s most successful office products.

qs.ex: mark one's pages 意為「在頁面上做記號」，用小紙片標記聖詩集的頁數，故選 (A) marked。
an idea occurred to sb. 意為「某人想到一個點子」，句型為「想法 + occur to + 人」，故選 (B) occurred to。
主要動詞 remembered 為過去式；關係子句 that everyone thought ___ a failure 中，everyone thought 為插入語，that 代替 glue 作空格動詞的主詞，敘述當時大家的看法，應用過去式 was，故選 (B) was。
空格後 you wanted it to 表示條件，「只要你想要它留著，它就留著」，故選 (C) as long as。
remove it without damage 意為「撕下它而不造成損壞」，故選 (D) without。

zh: 亞特．佛萊是 3M 公司的研究員。每個星期天他在教會唱詩班唱歌時，都為一件小小的煩心事所困擾。那就是，在他用小紙片在聖詩集上標記頁數之後，這些小紙片總是會掉得滿地都是。有一天，亞特．佛萊突然想到一個點子。他想起一位同事研發出的一種膠，大家都認為那是失敗品，因為它黏性不太好。於是他把這種膠塗在一張紙樣上，發現它不但是個很好的書籤，用來寫便條也很棒。只要你想要，它就會固定在原處；然後你可以把它撕下來而不造成損壞。這個產品後來被稱為便利貼，是 3M 最成功的辦公用品之一。
title: 便利貼的發明

text: The pineapple, long a symbol of Hawaii, was not a native plant. {{21}}, pineapples did not appear there until 1813. The pineapple was {{22}} found in Paraguay and in the southern part of Brazil. Natives planted the fruit across South and Central America and in the Caribbean region, {{23}} Christopher Columbus first found it. Columbus brought it, along with many other new things, back to Europe with him. From there, the tasty fruit {{24}} throughout other parts of civilization. It was carried on sailing ships around the world because it was found to help prevent scurvy, a disease that often {{25}} sailors on long voyages. It was at the end of one of these long voyages that the pineapple came to Hawaii to stay.

qs.ex: 前句說鳳梨不是原生植物，後句說 1813 年才出現，是用事實補強前句，故選 (B) In fact。
鳳梨「最初」是在巴拉圭和巴西南部被發現，指起源，故選 (C) originally。
先行詞為地點 the Caribbean region，後接完整子句 Columbus first found it，需用關係副詞 where，故選 (D) where。
句子描述哥倫布之後的歷史，主詞 the tasty fruit 缺過去式動詞，spread 的過去式與原形同形，故選 (A) spread。
a disease that bothers sailors 意為「困擾水手的疾病」；suffer 的主詞是受苦的一方（如 sailors suffer from a disease），疾病不能當 suffer 的主詞，故選 (A) bothered。

zh: 鳳梨長久以來是夏威夷的象徵，但它並不是當地原生的植物。事實上，鳳梨直到一八一三年才出現在那裡。鳳梨最初是在巴拉圭和巴西南部被發現的。原住民把這種水果種遍了南美洲、中美洲和加勒比海地區，哥倫布就是在那裡第一次發現它。哥倫布把它和許多其他新奇的東西一起帶回了歐洲。這種美味的水果再從歐洲傳遍了文明世界的其他地區。帆船把它載往世界各地，因為人們發現它有助於預防壞血病，這是一種常困擾長途航海水手的疾病。鳳梨正是在其中一趟長途航行的終點來到夏威夷，並在此落地生根。
title: 鳳梨傳入夏威夷

text: The Paralympics are Olympic-style games for athletes with a disability. They were organized for the first time in Rome in 1960. In Toronto in 1976, the idea of putting together different disability groups {{26}} sports competitions was born. Today, the Paralympics are sports events for athletes from six different disability groups. They emphasize the participants’ athletic achievements {{27}} their physical disability. The games have grown in size gradually. The number of athletes {{28}} in the Summer Paralympic Games has increased from 400 athletes from 23 countries in 1960 to 3,806 athletes from 136 countries in 2004.

The Paralympic Games have always been held in the same year as the Olympic Games. Since the Seoul 1988 Paralympic Games and the Albertville 1992 Winter Paralympic Games, they have also {{29}} in the same city as the Olympics. On June 19, 2001, an agreement was signed between the International Olympic Committee and the International Paralympics Committee to keep this {{30}} in the future. From the 2012 bid onwards, the city chosen to host the Olympic Games will also host the Paralympics.

qs.ex: the idea of putting together different disability groups for sports competitions，for 表「為了、用於」，故選 (A) for。
強調運動成就「而不是」身體障礙，instead of 表「而非」，故選 (B) instead of。
The number of athletes ___ in the Games：athletes 與 participate 為主動關係，用現在分詞 participating 後置修飾，故選 (C)。
have also taken place in the same city 意為「也在同一城市舉行」，take place 指舉行，故選 (B) taken place。
協議是要在未來「維持這項做法」（同一城市舉辦），practice 為「慣例、做法」，故選 (D) practice。

zh: 帕拉林匹克運動會是專為身心障礙運動員舉辦、仿照奧運形式的賽會。它於一九六○年首度在羅馬舉辦。一九七六年在多倫多，將不同障礙類別的族群集合起來參加運動競賽的構想誕生了。如今，帕拉林匹克運動會是為來自六種不同障礙類別的運動員所舉辦的體育賽事。它們強調參賽者的運動成就，而不是他們的身體障礙。這項賽會的規模逐漸成長。參加夏季帕拉林匹克運動會的運動員人數，已從一九六○年來自二十三個國家的四百名，增加到二○○四年來自一百三十六個國家的三千八百零六名。
帕拉林匹克運動會一直都與奧運在同一年舉行。自一九八八年漢城帕拉林匹克運動會與一九九二年阿爾貝維爾冬季帕拉林匹克運動會起，它們也都在與奧運相同的城市舉行。二○○一年六月十九日，國際奧林匹克委員會與國際帕拉林匹克委員會簽署了一項協議，要在未來持續這項做法。從二○一二年的申辦開始，獲選主辦奧運的城市也將主辦帕拉林匹克運動會。
title: 帕拉林匹克運動會

text: Familiar fables can be narrated differently or extended in interesting and humorous ways. The end of the famous fable of “The Tortoise and the Hare” is well known to all: the tortoise wins the race against the hare. The moral lesson is that slow and steady wins the race. We all have grown up with this popular version, but the {{31}} fable can be extended with different twists. At the request of the hare, a second race is {{32}} and this time, the hare runs without taking a rest and wins. The moral lesson is that {{33}} and consistent will always beat slow and steady. Then it is the tortoise that {{34}} the hare to a third race along a different route in which there is a river just before the final destination. This time, the tortoise wins the race because the hare cannot swim. The moral lesson is “First {{35}} your strengths, and then change the playing field to suit them.”

But the story continues. Both {{36}} know their own drawbacks and limitations very well; therefore, they jointly decide to have one last race—not to decide who the winner or loser is, but just for their own pleasure and satisfaction. The two {{37}} as a team. Firstly, the hare carries the tortoise on its back to the river. Then, the tortoise carries the hare and swims to the {{38}} bank of the river. Lastly, the hare carries the tortoise again on its back. Thus they reach the {{39}} line together. Overall, many moral lessons from the last match are highlighted. The most obvious one is the importance of {{40}}. Another moral which also means a great deal is “competition against situations rather than against rivals.”

qs.ex: the ___ fable 需形容詞，與前文 popular version 呼應，「同一則寓言」，故選 (I) same（形容詞）。
a second race is ___ 為被動語態，需過去分詞，應兔子要求「安排」第二場比賽，故選 (A) arranged（過去分詞）。
___ and consistent 與 consistent 並列，需形容詞，對比 slow，故選 (E) fast（形容詞）。
it is the tortoise that ___ the hare to a third race，that 子句缺動詞，主詞 tortoise 為單數，用現在式，challenge sb. to a race 意為「向某人挑戰比賽」，故選 (B) challenges（動詞）。
First ___ your strengths 為祈使句，需原形動詞，「找出自己的強項」，故選 (G) identify（原形動詞）。
Both ___ know 缺複數名詞作主詞，指烏龜與兔子兩位對手，故選 (C) competitors（名詞）。
The two ___ as a team 缺動詞，主詞 the two 為複數，用現在式，「合作」，故選 (D) cooperate（動詞）。
the ___ bank of the river 需形容詞，「對岸」，故選 (H) opposite（形容詞）。
the ___ line 需名詞性修飾語，the finishing line 即「終點線」，故選 (F) finishing（動名詞作修飾語）。
the importance of ___ 需名詞，兩者合作完成比賽，故選 (J) teamwork（名詞）。

zh: 大家熟悉的寓言可以用不同的方式敘述，或以有趣、幽默的方式延伸。〈龜兔賽跑〉這則著名寓言的結局眾所周知：烏龜贏了這場與兔子的比賽。其寓意是慢而穩者能贏得比賽。我們都是聽這個流行的版本長大的，但同一則寓言可以加上不同的轉折往下延伸。應兔子的要求，安排了第二場比賽，這次兔子一路不休息地跑，贏了比賽。其寓意是又快又持之以恆的人永遠勝過慢而穩的人。接著，輪到烏龜向兔子挑戰第三場比賽，路線不同，在終點前有一條河。這次烏龜贏了，因為兔子不會游泳。其寓意是：「先找出自己的強項，然後改變競賽場地以適合它們。」
但故事還沒完。兩位競爭者都非常清楚自己的缺點與限制，因此牠們共同決定進行最後一場比賽，不是要決定誰輸誰贏，而只是為了自己的樂趣與滿足。兩者以團隊的方式合作。首先，兔子背著烏龜到河邊。接著，烏龜背著兔子游到河的對岸。最後，兔子再度背著烏龜。就這樣，牠們一起抵達終點線。整體而言，最後這場比賽凸顯了許多寓意。最明顯的一個是團隊合作的重要性。另一個同樣意義重大的寓意是：「與情勢競爭，而不是與對手競爭。」
title: 龜兔賽跑續篇

text: Anita was shopping with her mother and enjoying it. Interestingly, both of them {{16}} buying the same pair of jeans.

According to a recent marketing study, young adults influence 88% of household clothing purchases. More often than not, those in their early twenties are the more {{17}} consumers. There isn’t a brand or a trend that these young people are not aware of. That is why mothers who want to keep abreast of trends usually {{18}} the experts－their daughters. This tells the retailers of the world that if you want to get into a mother’s {{19}}, you’ve got to win her daughter over first.

With a DJ playing various kinds of music rather than just rap, and a mix of clothing labels designed more for taste and fashion than for a precise age, department stores have managed to appeal to successful middle-aged women {{20}} losing their younger customers. They have created a shopping environment where the needs of both mother and daughter are satisfied.

qs.ex: end up + Ving 意為「最後（結果）做了……」，兩人最後買了同一款牛仔褲，故選 (B) ended up。
形容消費者「消息靈通的」，用 informed（見多識廣的）；informative 指提供資訊的，故選 (A) informed。
turn to sb. 意為「向某人求助」，媽媽向身為專家的女兒求助，故選 (C) turn to。
get into a mother's pocketbook 意為「讓媽媽掏錢」，pocketbook 指錢包，故選 (D) pocketbook。
managed to appeal to… without losing… 意為「吸引中年女性而不失去年輕顧客」，故選 (D) without。

zh: 安妮塔正和媽媽一起購物，而且逛得很開心。有趣的是，她們兩人最後都買了同一款牛仔褲。
根據最近一項行銷研究，年輕成人影響了百分之八十八的家庭服飾購買。二十出頭的人往往是消息較靈通的消費者。這些年輕人沒有不知道的品牌或流行趨勢。這就是為什麼想跟上潮流的媽媽們，通常會向專家，也就是她們的女兒求助。這告訴全世界的零售商，如果你想讓媽媽掏錢，就得先爭取她女兒的支持。
百貨公司請 DJ 播放各種類型的音樂，而不只是饒舌樂，並混合陳列更重品味與時尚、而非針對特定年齡所設計的服飾品牌，因而成功吸引了有成就的中年女性，同時又不失去較年輕的顧客。它們營造出一個能同時滿足母女雙方需求的購物環境。
title: 母女共同購物

text: Onions can be divided into two categories: fresh onions and storage onions. Fresh onions are available {{21}} yellow, red and white throughout their season, March through August. They can be {{22}} by their thin, light-colored skin. Because they have a higher water content, they are typically sweeter and milder tasting than storage onions. This higher water content also makes {{23}} easier for them to bruise. With its delicate taste, the fresh onion is an ideal choice for salads and other lightly-cooked dishes. Storage onions, on the other hand, are available August through April. {{24}} fresh onions, they have multiple layers of thick, dark, papery skin. They also have an {{25}} flavor and a higher percentage of solids. For these reasons, storage onions are the best choice for spicy dishes that require longer cooking times or more flavor.

qs.ex: be available in + 顏色／尺寸 意為「有……顏色可供選擇」，故選 (C) in。
be identified by 意為「憑……被辨識出來」，以薄的淺色外皮辨認，故選 (C) identified。
make it + 形容詞 + to V，it 為形式受詞，真正受詞為 to bruise，故選 (D) it。
前文說新鮮洋蔥外皮薄，此處說儲藏洋蔥有多層厚皮，兩者相反，Unlike fresh onions 意為「與新鮮洋蔥不同」，故選 (A) Unlike。
與新鮮洋蔥的溫和相對，儲藏洋蔥味道較「濃烈」，intense flavor，故選 (B) intense。

zh: 洋蔥可分為兩類：新鮮洋蔥與儲藏洋蔥。新鮮洋蔥在三月到八月的產季中，有黃色、紅色和白色的可供選擇。它們可以憑薄而淺色的外皮辨識出來。由於含水量較高，它們通常比儲藏洋蔥更甜、味道更溫和。較高的含水量也使它們更容易碰傷。新鮮洋蔥味道細緻，是做沙拉和其他稍加烹調菜餚的理想食材。另一方面，儲藏洋蔥在八月到四月之間供應。與新鮮洋蔥不同，它們有多層厚而顏色深的紙質外皮。它們的味道也較濃烈，固形物含量的比例也較高。基於這些原因，烹調需要較長時間或較重風味的辛辣菜餚時，儲藏洋蔥是最佳選擇。
title: 新鮮洋蔥與儲藏洋蔥

text: Many people like to drink bottled water because they feel that tap water may not be safe, but is bottled water really any better?

Bottled water is mostly sold in plastic bottles and that’s why it is potentially health {{26}}. Processing the plastic can lead to the release of harmful chemical substances into the water contained in the bottles. The chemicals can be absorbed into the body and {{27}} physical discomfort, such as stomach cramps and diarrhea.

Health risks can also result from inappropriate storage of bottled water. Bacteria can multiply if the water is kept on the shelves for too long or if it is exposed to heat or direct sunlight. {{28}} the information on storage and shipment is not always readily available to consumers, bottled water may not be a better alternative to tap water.

Besides these {{29}} issues, bottled water has other disadvantages. It contributes to global warming. An estimated 2.5 million tons of carbon dioxide were generated in 2006 by the production of plastic for bottled water. In addition, bottled water produces an incredible amount of solid {{30}}. According to one research, 90% of the bottles used are not recycled and lie for ages in landfills.

qs.ex: health-threatening 意為「威脅健康的」，與後文有害化學物質呼應，故選 (B) threatening。
can be absorbed… and ___：與 can 後的 be absorbed 並列，助動詞 can 後接原形動詞，故選 (A) cause。
後句 bottled water may not be a better alternative 是因為資訊不易取得，表示原因，連接子句用 Since，故選 (C) Since。
these ___ issues 指前面談的健康風險，即安全問題，故選 (D) safety。
瓶子不被回收、堆在掩埋場，solid waste 意為「固體廢棄物」，故選 (A) waste。

zh: 許多人喜歡喝瓶裝水，因為他們覺得自來水可能不安全，但瓶裝水真的比較好嗎？
瓶裝水大多裝在塑膠瓶中販售，這就是它可能威脅健康的原因。塑膠的加工過程可能導致有害化學物質釋放到瓶內的水中。這些化學物質會被人體吸收，並引起身體不適，例如胃痙攣和腹瀉。
瓶裝水若儲存不當，也會造成健康風險。如果水放在架上太久，或暴露在高溫或陽光直射下，細菌就會繁殖。由於消費者不一定能輕易取得有關儲存與運送的資訊，瓶裝水未必是比自來水更好的替代品。
除了這些安全問題之外，瓶裝水還有其他缺點。它會加劇全球暖化。據估計，二○○六年光是生產瓶裝水用的塑膠，就產生了二百五十萬噸的二氧化碳。此外，瓶裝水還製造了數量驚人的固體廢棄物。根據一項研究，所使用的瓶子有百分之九十沒有被回收，長年躺在掩埋場裡。
title: 瓶裝水的隱憂

text: Football is more than a sport; it is also an invaluable {{31}}. In teaching young players to cooperate with their fellows on the practice {{32}}, the game shows them the necessity of teamwork in society. It prepares them to be {{33}} citizens and persons.

Wherever football is played, the players learn the rough-and-tumble lesson that only through the {{34}} of each member can the team win. It is a lesson they must always {{35}} on the field. Off the field, they continue to keep it in mind. In society, the former player does not look upon himself as a lone wolf who has the right to remain {{36}} from the society and go his own way. He understands his place in the team; he knows he is a member of society and must {{37}} himself as such. He realizes that only by cooperating can he do his {{38}} in making society what it should be. The man who has played football knows that teamwork is {{39}} in modern living. He is also aware that every citizen must do his part if the nation is to {{40}}. So he has little difficulty in adjusting himself to his role in family life and in the business world, and to his duties as a citizen.

qs.ex: an invaluable ___ 需名詞，足球教導年輕人團隊合作，扮演「老師」角色，故選 (C) teacher（名詞）。
the practice ___ 需名詞，practice field 指「練習場」，故選 (I) field（名詞）。
to be ___ citizens 需形容詞，「更好的」公民，故選 (G) better（形容詞）。
the ___ of each member 需名詞，只有靠每位成員的合作，球隊才能獲勝，故選 (A) cooperation（名詞）。
must always ___ 前有助動詞，需原形動詞，「記住」這個教訓，後文 keep it in mind 呼應，故選 (J) remember（原形動詞）。
remain ___ from the society 需形容詞或過去分詞，「與社會隔絕」，故選 (E) isolated（過去分詞作形容詞）。
must ___ himself as such 需原形動詞，behave oneself as 意為「以……身分行事」，故選 (D) behave（原形動詞）。
do his ___ 需名詞，do one's share 意為「盡自己的一份力」，故選 (H) share（名詞）。
teamwork is ___ in modern living 需形容詞，團隊合作在現代生活中「不可或缺」，故選 (F) essential（形容詞）。
if the nation is to ___ 需原形動詞，國家若要「繁榮」，故選 (B) prosper（原形動詞）。

zh: 足球不只是一項運動，它還是一位無價的老師。在教導年輕球員於練習場上與同伴合作的過程中，這項運動讓他們明白社會中團隊合作的必要性。它幫助他們做好準備，成為更好的公民，也成為更好的人。

不論在哪裡踢足球，球員們都會在激烈的拚搏中學到這個教訓：只有靠每位成員的合作，球隊才能獲勝。這是他們在球場上必須時時記得的一課。離開球場後，他們仍把它放在心上。在社會中，曾經踢過球的人不會把自己看成是一匹孤狼，以為自己有權與社會隔絕、獨行其是。他明白自己在團隊中的位置；他知道自己是社會的一分子，必須以此身分來行事。他體認到，只有透過合作，他才能盡一份力，讓社會成為它應有的樣貌。踢過足球的人知道，團隊合作在現代生活中是不可或缺的。他也明白，如果國家要繁榮，每位公民都必須盡自己的本分。因此，他在適應自己在家庭生活和職場上的角色，以及身為公民的職責時，幾乎沒有困難。
title: 足球的社會教育

text: When it comes to Egypt, people think of pyramids and mummies, both of which are closely related to Egyptian religious beliefs. The ancient Egyptians believed firmly in life {{16}} death. When a person died, his or her soul was thought to travel to an underworld, where it {{17}} a series of judgments before it could progress to a better life in the next world. For the soul to travel smoothly, the body had to {{18}} unharmed. Thus, they learned how to preserve the body by drying it out, oiling and then {{19}} the body in linen, before placing it in the coffin. Egyptians also built pyramids as {{20}} for their kings, or pharaohs. The pyramid housed the pharaoh’s body together with priceless treasure, which would accompany him into the next world.

qs.ex: believe in life after death 意為「相信死後有生命」，故選 (C) after。
go through a series of judgments 意為「經歷一連串審判」，且 was thought to 的敘述為過去，用過去式，故選 (A) went through。
the body had to remain unharmed 意為「身體必須保持完好」，remain + 形容詞，故選 (A) remain。
by drying…, oiling and then ___ 為介系詞 by 後的動名詞並列，故選 (B) wrapping。
金字塔安放法老遺體與珍寶，是國王的「陵墓」，故選 (D) tombs。

zh: 提到埃及，人們會想到金字塔和木乃伊，兩者都與埃及人的宗教信仰密切相關。古埃及人堅信人死後仍有生命。他們認為，人死之後，靈魂會前往冥界，在那裡經歷一連串的審判，之後才能進入來世更美好的生活。為了讓靈魂順利旅行，身體必須保持完好無損。因此，他們學會了保存遺體的方法：先將遺體風乾、塗油，再用亞麻布包裹，然後放入棺木。埃及人也為他們的國王，即法老，建造金字塔作為陵墓。金字塔安放著法老的遺體以及無價的珍寶，這些珍寶將陪伴他進入來世。
title: 古埃及的來世信仰

text: On March 23, 1999, the musical MAMMA MIA! made its first public appearance in London. It {{21}} the kind of welcome it has been getting ever since. The audience went wild. They were literally out of their seats and singing and dancing in the aisles.

MAMMA MIA! has become a {{22}} entertainment phenomenon. More than 30 million people all over the world have fallen in love with the characters, the story and the music. The musical has been performed in more than nine languages, with more productions than any {{23}} musical. Its worldwide popularity is mainly due to its theme music, which showcases ABBA’s timeless songs in a fresh and vital way {{24}} retains the essence of both pop music and good musical theater. It has {{25}} so many people that a film version was also made. To no one’s surprise, it has enjoyed similar popularity.

qs.ex: 主詞 It 指音樂劇，be given a welcome 意為「受到歡迎」，要用被動；且指 1999 年首演的過去情況，故選 (B) was given。
more than 30 million people all over the world，表示全球性的現象，global entertainment phenomenon，故選 (B) global。
more… than any other + 單數名詞，意為「比任何其他……都多」，故選 (C) other。
空格前的 a fresh and vital way 為先行詞，後接 retains…，需關係代名詞作主詞，用 that，故選 (D) that。
appeal to sb. 意為「吸引某人」，吸引了許多人才改編為電影，故選 (A) appealed to。

zh: 一九九九年三月二十三日，音樂劇《媽媽咪呀！》在倫敦首度公開演出。它當時受到的歡迎，此後一直延續至今。觀眾瘋狂不已，他們真的離開座位，在走道上又唱又跳。
《媽媽咪呀！》已成為一個全球性的娛樂現象。全世界有三千多萬人愛上了劇中的角色、故事與音樂。這齣音樂劇已用九種以上的語言演出，製作的版本數量比任何其他音樂劇都多。它能風靡全球，主要歸功於它的主題音樂，以清新而有活力的方式展現阿巴合唱團歷久彌新的歌曲，同時保留了流行音樂與優秀音樂劇的精髓。它吸引了這麼多人，以至於還拍成了電影版。毫不令人意外，電影版也同樣大受歡迎。
title: 音樂劇《媽媽咪呀！》

text: Which is more valuable? Water or diamonds? Water is more useful to mankind than diamonds, and yet {{26}} are costlier. Why? Called the diamond-water paradox, this is a classic problem posed to students of economics.

The answer has to do with supply and demand. Being a rare natural resource, diamonds are {{27}} in supply. However, their demand is high because many people buy them to tell the world that they have money, {{28}} as conspicuous consumption in economics. In other words, the scarcity of goods is {{29}} causes humans to attribute value. If we {{30}} surrounded by an unending abundance of diamonds, we probably wouldn’t value them very much. Hence, diamonds carry a higher monetary value than water, even though we find more use for water.

qs.ex: 前面提到兩樣東西 Water or diamonds，the latter 指後者，即鑽石，鑽石比水貴，故選 (D) the latter。
因為鑽石是稀有資源，供給「有限」，後面 However 與高需求對比，故選 (C) limited。
空格前為完整子句，後為 as conspicuous consumption，過去分詞 termed 作補充說明，意為「被稱為」，故選 (B) termed。
the scarcity of goods is what causes… 為關係代名詞 what 引導的名詞子句作補語，意為「正是……」，故選 (A) what。
If we ___ surrounded… we probably wouldn't 為與現在事實相反的假設，if 子句用過去式 were，故選 (D) were。

zh: 哪一個比較有價值？水還是鑽石？水對人類比鑽石更有用，然而後者卻更昂貴。為什麼？這被稱為鑽石與水的矛盾，是拋給經濟學學生的一個經典問題。
答案和供給與需求有關。鑽石是一種稀有的天然資源，供給有限。然而，它的需求很高，因為許多人購買鑽石是為了向世人宣告自己有錢，這在經濟學中被稱為炫耀性消費。換句話說，正是商品的稀少性使人類賦予它價值。如果我們被無窮無盡的鑽石所包圍，我們大概就不會很重視它們。因此，儘管我們覺得水更有用，鑽石的貨幣價值卻比水高。
title: 鑽石與水的矛盾

text: Popcorn is one of the snacks that rarely fail to make watching a movie more fun. However, the modern way of preparing this {{31}} snack may carry an unhappy secret. Research by the U.S. government now reports that microwave popcorn may contain substances that can cause health {{32}}.

Researchers found that commercial popcorn companies often coat their microwave popcorn bags with a {{33}} called perfluorooctanoic acid (PFOA) which has been found to cause both cancer and lung disease in laboratory animals. Making matters worse, the artificial butter substitute that generally {{34}} with microwavable popcorn contains a common food-flavoring substance. This substance, according to health scientists, is {{35}} for some serious lung diseases.

For an easy and {{36}} alternative, nutritionists suggest that we pop our own popcorn. All that is {{37}} is a large, high pot, about four tablespoons of vegetable oil and a small handful of organic popcorn kernels. When the kernels start {{38}}, shake the pot to let the steam escape and to let the unpopped kernels fall to the bottom. As soon as the popping slows down, {{39}} the pot from the stove. Then pour the popcorn into a bowl and season with a small {{40}} of real butter or olive oil and natural salt. And the healthy and fun snack is ready to serve.

qs.ex: this ___ snack 需形容詞修飾 snack，開頭說爆米花是常見、受大眾喜愛的零食，故選 (D) popular（形容詞）。
cause health ___ 需名詞（複數），health problems 意為「健康問題」，故選 (J) problems（名詞）。
a ___ called PFOA 需名詞，PFOA 是一種化學物質，故選 (A) chemical（名詞）。
that generally ___ with microwavable popcorn，先行詞 substitute 為單數，需第三人稱單數動詞，come with 意為「附帶」，故選 (E) comes（動詞）。
be responsible for 意為「是……的原因」，後接 for some serious lung diseases，故選 (H) responsible（形容詞）。
an easy and ___ alternative 需形容詞，與 easy 並列，對比前文有害的微波爆米花，故選 (F) healthy（形容詞）。
All that is ___ 為 All (that is needed)，被動語態需過去分詞，故選 (G) needed（過去分詞）。
start ___ 後接動名詞或不定詞，玉米粒開始「爆開」，故選 (C) popping（動名詞）。
As soon as… slows down, ___ the pot 為祈使句，需原形動詞，將鍋子從爐子上移開，故選 (I) remove（原形動詞）。
a small ___ of real butter 需名詞，a small amount of 意為「少量的」，故選 (B) amount（名詞）。

zh: 爆米花是幾乎總能讓看電影更有趣的零食之一。然而，現代人製作這種熱門零食的方式，可能藏著一個令人不快的祕密。美國政府的研究現在指出，微波爆米花可能含有會造成健康問題的物質。
研究人員發現，商業爆米花公司常在微波爆米花的包裝袋上塗一種稱為全氟辛酸（PFOA）的化學物質，這種物質已被發現會使實驗動物罹患癌症和肺部疾病。更糟的是，微波爆米花通常附帶的人造奶油替代品，含有一種常見的食品調味物質。根據健康科學家的說法，這種物質是某些嚴重肺部疾病的元凶。
營養學家建議我們自己爆爆米花，作為一種簡單又健康的替代做法。所需要的只是一個又大又高的鍋子、約四大匙的植物油，以及一小把有機爆米花玉米粒。當玉米粒開始爆開時，搖動鍋子讓蒸氣散出，並讓未爆開的玉米粒掉到鍋底。一旦爆裂聲漸漸稀疏，就立刻把鍋子從爐子上移開。然後把爆米花倒進碗裡，加入少量真正的奶油或橄欖油以及天然鹽調味。這份健康又有趣的零食就可以上桌了。
title: 微波爆米花的隱憂

text: Kizhi is an island on Lake Onega in Karelia, Russia, with a beautiful collection of wooden churches and houses. It is one of the most popular tourist {{16}} in Russia and a United Nations Educational, Scientific, and Cultural Organization (UNESCO) World Heritage Site.
The island is about 7 km long and 0.5 km wide. It is surrounded by about 5,000 other islands, some of {{17}} are just rocks sticking out of the ground.

The entire island of Kizhi is, {{18}}, an outdoor museum of wooden architecture created in 1966. It contains many historically significant and beautiful wooden structures, {{19}} windmills, boathouses, chapels, fish houses, and homes. The jewel of the architecture is the 22-domed Transfiguration Church, built in the early 1700s. It is about 37 m tall, {{20}} it one of the tallest log structures in the world. The church was built with pine trees brought from the mainland, which was quite common for the 18th century.

qs.ex: tourist attractions 為「觀光景點」的固定搭配，故選 attractions。
空格前為 some of，後接子句，需用「介系詞＋關係代名詞」引導非限定子句，故選 which（some of which）。
本句說整座島就是一座博物館，空格處用來補充強調事實，in fact（事實上）最合適。
後面列舉的 windmills 等是前面 structures 的實例，including（包括）正確；besides 是「除…之外還有」，語意不合。
空格前已有完整子句，後接 it one of the tallest，用現在分詞 making 表示結果（分詞構句）。

zh: 基日島位於俄羅斯卡累利阿的奧涅加湖上，擁有一批美麗的木造教堂與房屋。它是俄羅斯最熱門的觀光景點之一，也是聯合國教育科學及文化組織（UNESCO）的世界遺產。
這座島長約七公里、寬約半公里，周圍環繞著大約五千座其他島嶼，其中有些只是露出地面的岩石。
事實上，整座基日島就是一座成立於 1966 年的木造建築戶外博物館。島上有許多具歷史意義且美麗的木造建築，包括風車、船屋、小禮拜堂、魚屋與民宅。這些建築中的瑰寶，是擁有 22 個圓頂的主顯聖容教堂，建於 1700 年代初期。教堂高約 37 公尺，因而成為世界上最高的原木建築之一。這座教堂是用從本土運來的松木建成，這在十八世紀相當普遍。
title: 俄羅斯基日島木造建築

text: There was once a time when all human beings were gods. However, they often took their divinity for granted and {{21}} abused it. Seeing this, Brahma, the chief god, decided to take their divinity away from them and hide it {{22}} it could never be found.

Brahma called a council of the gods to help him decide on a place to hide the divinity. The gods suggested that they hide it {{23}} in the earth or take it to the top of the highest mountain. But Brahma thought {{24}} would do because he believed humans would dig into the earth and climb every mountain, and eventually find it. So, the gods gave up.

Brahma thought for a long time and finally decided to hide their divinity in the center of their own being, for humans would never think to {{25}} it there. Since that time humans have been going up and down the earth, digging, climbing, and exploring—searching for something already within themselves.

qs.ex: even abused 表示「甚至濫用」，承接 took for granted 作遞進，故選 even。
hide it where it could never be found 為地方副詞子句，where 引導，意為「藏在永遠找不到的地方」。
與後面的 in the earth 搭配，deep in the earth（深埋在地底）最自然。
前面兩個提議（藏在地底、山頂）都被否決，故用 neither（兩者皆不）。
人類想不到去「尋找」神性，look for 符合語意；bump into 為偶然遇到，不合。

zh: 從前有一個時代，所有人類都是神。然而他們常把自己的神性視為理所當然，甚至濫用它。看到這種情形，眾神之首婆羅賀摩決定把人類的神性拿走，藏在一個永遠找不到的地方。
婆羅賀摩召集眾神開會，請大家幫忙決定藏匿神性的地點。眾神建議把它深埋在地底，或帶到最高山的山頂。但婆羅賀摩認為這兩個地方都不行，因為他相信人類會挖掘大地、攀登每一座山，最後還是會找到。於是眾神放棄了。
婆羅賀摩想了很久，最後決定把人類的神性藏在他們自己的內心深處，因為人類絕不會想到要到那裡去找。從那時起，人類就一直上天下地，挖掘、攀登、探索，尋找著原本就在自己內心的東西。
title: 婆羅賀摩藏起人類的神性

text: In the fall of 1973, in an effort to bring attention to the conflict between Egypt and Israel, World Hello Day was born. The objective is to promote peace all over the world, and to {{26}} barriers between every nationality. Since then, World Hello Day—November 21st of every year—{{27}} observed by people in 180 countries.

Taking part couldn’t be {{28}}. All one has to do is say hello to 10 people on the day. However, in response to the {{29}} of this event, the concepts of fostering peace and harmony do not have to be confined to one day a year. We can {{30}} the spirit going by communicating often and consciously. It is a simple act that anyone can do and it reminds us that communication is more effective than conflict.

qs.ex: barriers（隔閡）應被「打破」，break down barriers 為常見搭配。
Since then 引導的句子需用現在完成式，主詞為單數 Day，被動語態 has been observed。
Taking part couldn’t be easier 為「再簡單不過」的比較級慣用語；後句說只要向十個人問好，正與此呼應。
in response to the aim of this event（針對此活動的宗旨）；後文說和平理念不必侷限一天，語意承接。
keep the spirit going（讓這種精神持續下去）為固定用法。

zh: 1973 年秋天，為了讓世人注意埃及與以色列之間的衝突，世界問候日誕生了。其目的是在全世界促進和平，並打破各民族之間的隔閡。從那時起，世界問候日（每年 11 月 21 日）就有 180 個國家的人民一起慶祝。
參與再簡單不過了：當天只要向十個人說聲哈囉。不過，就這個活動的宗旨而言，促進和平與和諧的理念並不需要侷限於一年中的一天。我們可以藉由經常而用心地溝通，讓這種精神延續下去。這是任何人都做得到的簡單舉動，它提醒我們溝通比衝突更有效。
title: 世界問候日

text: Generally there are two ways to name typhoons: the number-based convention and the list-based convention. Following the number-based convention, typhoons are coded with {{31}} types of numbers such as a 4-digit or a 6-digit code. For example, the 14th typhoon in 2003 can be labeled either as Typhoon 0314 or Typhoon 200314. The {{32}} of this convention, however, is that a number is hard to remember. The list-based convention, on the other hand, is based on the list of typhoon names compiled in advance by a committee, and is more widely used.

At the very beginning, only {{33}} names were used because at that time typhoons were named after girlfriends or wives of the experts on the committee. In 1979, however, male names were also included because women protested against the original naming {{34}} for reasons of gender equality.

In Asia, Western names were used until 2000 when the committee decided to use Asian names to {{35}} Asians’ awareness of typhoons. The names were chosen from a name pool {{36}} of 140 names, 10 each from the 14 members of the committee. Each country has its unique naming preferences. Korea and Japan {{37}} animal names and China likes names of gods such as Longwang (dragon king) and Fengshen (god of the wind).

After the 140 names are all used in order, they will be {{38}}. But the names can be changed. If a member country suffers great damage from a certain typhoon, it can {{39}} that the name of the typhoon be deleted from the list at the annual committee meeting. For example, the names of Nabi by South Korea, and Longwang by China were {{40}} with other names in 2007. The deletion of both names was due to the severe damage caused by the typhoons bearing the names.

qs.ex: 修飾複數名詞 types，需形容詞，various types of numbers（各種數字）。
冠詞 The 後接名詞，後句 a number is hard to remember 說明缺點，故選名詞 disadvantage。
因為早期以女友、妻子命名，且後文說 male names were also included，可知當時只有 female names（形容詞）。
naming practice（命名慣例）為名詞，指原本的命名做法。
to 後接原形動詞，raise awareness（提高意識）為搭配。
name pool composed of 140 names，過去分詞作後置修飾，composed of（由…組成）。
主詞 Korea and Japan 為複數，空格需不加 -s 的現在式動詞，favor 在此為動詞「偏愛」，與後句 China likes 呼應。
names 用完後會被 recycled（循環再用），be 動詞後接過去分詞。
助動詞 can 後接原形動詞，request 在此為動詞，後接 that 子句，子句內用原形動詞 be deleted（省略 should）。
名字被刪除後以其他名字 replaced（取代），be replaced with 為固定用法。

zh: 一般來說，颱風有兩種命名方式：編號制與名單制。依編號制，颱風以各種數字編碼，例如四位數或六位數的代碼。舉例來說，2003 年的第 14 號颱風可以標示為 0314 號颱風或 200314 號颱風。不過，這種制度的缺點是數字很難記。相對地，名單制則是依據委員會事先編好的颱風名單，使用得更為普遍。
最初只使用女性名字，因為當時颱風是以委員會專家的女友或妻子來命名。然而到了 1979 年，也加入了男性名字，因為女性基於性別平等的理由抗議原本的命名做法。
在亞洲，直到 2000 年之前都使用西方名字，那年委員會決定改用亞洲名字，以提高亞洲人對颱風的警覺。這些名字選自一個由 140 個名字組成的名單庫，由委員會的 14 個成員各提供 10 個。每個國家都有自己獨特的命名偏好：韓國與日本偏愛動物名稱，中國則喜歡龍王、風神之類神明的名字。
140 個名字依序用完後，會再循環使用。但名字是可以更換的。如果某個會員國因某個颱風而遭受重大損害，可以在每年的委員會會議上要求把該颱風的名字從名單中刪除。例如在 2007 年，南韓提出的 Nabi 與中國提出的龍王就被其他名字取代。這兩個名字被刪除，都是因為使用這些名字的颱風造成嚴重災害。
title: 颱風的命名方式

text: An area code is a section of a telephone number which generally represents the geographical area that the phone receiving the call is based in. It is the two or three digits just before the local number. If the number {{16}} is in the same area as the number making the call, an area code usually doesn’t need to be dialed. The local number, {{17}}, must always be dialed in its entirety.

The area code was introduced in the United States in 1947. It was created {{18}} the format of XYX, with X being any number between 2-9 and Y being either 1 or 0. Cities and areas with higher populations would have a smaller first and third digit, and 1 as the center digit. New York, being the largest city in the United States, was {{19}} the 212 area code, followed by Los Angeles at 213.

In countries other than the United States and Canada, the area code generally determines the {{20}} of a call. Calls within an area code and often a small group of neighboring area codes are normally charged at a lower rate than outside the area code.

qs.ex: the number 與 call 為被動關係，分詞片語 being called 修飾 number（被撥打的號碼）。
前句說區碼通常不需撥，本句說市話號碼則必須全撥，語氣相對，用 on the other hand。
created in the format of XYX 表示「以…格式」，介系詞 in 搭配 format。
be assigned the 212 area code（被分配到 212 區碼）；assign 可接雙受詞，被動後保留一個受詞。
後句說區碼內通話費率較低，可知區碼決定通話的 cost（費用）。

zh: 區域號碼是電話號碼的一部分，通常代表受話方電話所在的地理區域。它是位於市內號碼之前的兩位或三位數字。如果被撥打的號碼和撥出電話的號碼位於同一區域，通常不需要撥區域號碼。另一方面，市內號碼則一定要完整撥出。
區域號碼於 1947 年在美國開始使用。它是以 XYX 的格式設計的，其中 X 是 2 到 9 之間的任何數字，Y 則是 1 或 0。人口較多的城市與地區，第一與第三位數字較小，中間數字為 1。紐約是美國最大的城市，因此分配到 212 區碼，其次是洛杉磯的 213。
在美國與加拿大以外的國家，區域號碼通常決定通話的費用。在同一區碼內（往往也包括鄰近的幾個區碼）通話，收費通常比打到區碼以外來得低。
title: 電話區域號碼

text: For coin collectors who invest money in coins, the value of a coin is determined by various factors. First, scarcity is a major determinant. {{21}} a coin is, the more it is worth. Note, however, that rarity has little to do with the {{22}} of a coin. Many thousand-year-old coins often sell for no more than a few dollars because there are a lot of them around, {{23}} a 1913 Liberty Head Nickel may sell for over one million US dollars because there are only five in existence.

Furthermore, the demand for a particular coin will also {{24}} influence coin values. Some coins may command higher prices because they are more popular with collectors. For example, a 1798 dime is much rarer than a 1916 dime, but the {{25}} sells for significantly more, simply because many more people collect early 20th century dimes than dimes from the 1700s.

qs.ex: the more it is worth 為「the＋比較級，the＋比較級」句型，前半也需 The rarer。
後文千年古幣只賣幾元，說明稀有度與錢幣的年齡（age）無太大關係。
前後兩句是對比：千年古幣便宜，而 1913 鎳幣很貴，用 while 表示對比。
also greatly influence 表示「也大大影響」；hardly 與 also 語意相反。
兩個年份的硬幣，賣得貴的是後提到的 1916 年者，用 the latter 指稱。

zh: 對於投資錢幣的收藏家來說，錢幣的價值由各種因素決定。首先，稀少性是主要的決定因素。錢幣越稀有，價值越高。不過要注意，稀有程度與錢幣的年代沒什麼關係。許多千年古幣往往只賣幾塊錢，因為它們的數量很多；而 1913 年的自由女神頭像五分錢幣卻可能賣到一百萬美元以上，因為現存只有五枚。
此外，對特定錢幣的需求也會大大影響錢幣價值。有些錢幣因為較受收藏家歡迎，可能賣得較高價。例如，1798 年的一角硬幣比 1916 年的稀有得多，但後者卻賣得貴很多，只是因為收集二十世紀初一角硬幣的人比收集 1700 年代一角硬幣的人多得多。
title: 錢幣的價值

text: French psychologist Alfred Binet (1859-1911) took a different approach from most other psychologists of his day: He was interested in the workings of the {{26}} mind rather than the nature of mental illness. He wanted to find a way to measure the ability to think and reason, apart from education in any particular field. In 1905 he developed a test in which he {{27}} children do tasks such as follow commands, copy patterns, name objects, and put things in order or arrange them properly. He later created a standard of measuring children’s intelligence {{28}} the data he had collected from the French children he studied. If 70 percent of 8-year-olds could pass a particular test, then {{29}} on the test represented an 8-year-old’s level of intelligence. From Binet’s work, the phrase “intelligence quotient” (“IQ”) entered the English vocabulary. The IQ is the ratio of “mental age” to chronological age times 100, with 100 {{30}} the average. So, an 8-year-old who passes the 10-year-old’s test would have an IQ of 10/8 times 100, or 125.

qs.ex: 與 mental illness 相對，他研究的是正常的心智（normal mind）。
空格後接原形動詞 do，使役動詞 had＋受詞＋原形，表示「讓孩子去做（測驗中的）各項任務」。
標準是根據他蒐集的資料而建立，be based on 的分詞形式 based on（以…為基礎）。
70% 的八歲兒童能通過，則在該測驗上的 success（成功／通過）代表八歲的智力水準。
with 100 being the average 為 with 的獨立分詞構句，用 being。

zh: 法國心理學家阿爾弗雷德·比奈（1859–1911）採取了與同時代大多數心理學家不同的研究取向：他感興趣的是正常心智的運作，而不是心理疾病的本質。他想找出一種方法，來測量思考與推理的能力，並且不受任何特定領域教育的影響。1905 年，他設計了一個測驗，讓孩子們去完成一些任務，例如依指令行動、模仿圖案、說出物品名稱，以及把東西排好順序或適當地排列。後來他根據從所研究的法國兒童身上蒐集到的資料，建立了一套衡量兒童智力的標準。如果有 70% 的八歲兒童能通過某項測驗，那麼通過這項測驗就代表八歲兒童的智力水準。從比奈的研究中，「智力商數」（IQ）一詞進入了英語詞彙。智商是「心智年齡」與實際年齡的比值乘以 100，而 100 為平均值。因此，一個通過十歲兒童測驗的八歲孩子，智商就是 10/8 乘以 100，即 125。
title: 比奈與智商測驗

text: Often called “rainforests of the sea,” coral reefs provide a home for 25% of all species in the ocean. They are stony structures full of dark hideaways where fish and sea animals can lay their eggs and {{31}} from predators. Without these underwater “apartment houses,” there would be fewer fish in the ocean. Some species might even become {{32}} or disappear completely.

There are thousands of reefs in the world; {{33}}, however, they are now in serious danger. More than one-third are in such bad shape that they could die within ten years. Many might not even {{34}} that long! Scientists are working hard to find out what leads to this destruction. There are still a lot of questions unanswered, but three main causes have been {{35}}.

The first cause is pollution on land. The pollutants run with rainwater into rivers and streams, which {{36}} the poisons into the ocean. Chemicals from the poisons kill reefs or make them weak, so they have less {{37}} to diseases.

Global warming is another reason. Higher ocean temperatures kill the important food source for the coral—the algae, the tiny greenish-gold water plants that live on coral. When the algae die, the coral loses its color and it also dies {{38}}. This process, known as “coral bleaching,” has happened more and more frequently in recent years.

The last factor contributing to the {{39}} of coral reefs is people. People sometimes crash into reefs with their boats or drop anchors on them, breaking off large chunks of coral. Divers who walk on reefs can also do serious damage. Moreover, some people even break coral off to collect for {{40}} since it is so colorful and pretty.
How can we help the reefs? We need to learn more about them and work together to stop the activities that may threaten their existence.

qs.ex: 與 lay their eggs 並列的動詞原形，escape from predators（躲避掠食者）。
become 後接形容詞，endangered（瀕臨絕種的）與 disappear completely 並列。
sadly 為修飾整句的副詞，意為「令人遺憾的是」，與插入語 however 一起表示語氣轉折。
might not even last that long（甚至撐不了那麼久），last 作不及物動詞「持續」，助動詞後接原形。
三個主要原因已被 identified（查明），have been 後接過去分詞。
關係代名詞 which 指 rivers and streams，動詞用 carry the poisons（把毒物帶入海洋）。
less resistance to diseases（對疾病的抵抗力較弱），需名詞。
珊瑚失去顏色後，最終（eventually）也會死亡，副詞修飾 dies。
the disappearance of coral reefs（珊瑚礁的消失），the 後接名詞。
to collect for souvenirs（收集作紀念品），for 後接名詞複數。

zh: 珊瑚礁常被稱為「海洋的雨林」，為海洋中 25% 的物種提供棲身之處。它們是布滿昏暗藏身處的岩石結構，魚類與海洋動物可以在那裡產卵並躲避掠食者。沒有這些水下的「公寓大樓」，海裡的魚會變少，有些物種甚至可能瀕臨絕種或完全消失。
世界上有數千座珊瑚礁；然而令人遺憾的是，它們現在正處於嚴重的危機中。超過三分之一的珊瑚礁狀況非常糟，可能在十年內死亡。許多甚至可能撐不了那麼久！科學家正努力找出導致這種破壞的原因。仍有許多問題沒有答案，但已經查明了三個主要原因。
第一個原因是陸地上的污染。污染物隨著雨水流入河川與溪流，河水再把毒物帶進海洋。毒物中的化學物質會殺死珊瑚礁，或使它們變得虛弱，因此對疾病的抵抗力變差。
全球暖化是另一個原因。海水溫度升高會殺死珊瑚的重要食物來源，也就是藻類，一種附著在珊瑚上、呈綠金色的微小水生植物。藻類死亡時，珊瑚會失去顏色，最終也會死亡。這個過程稱為「珊瑚白化」，近年來發生得越來越頻繁。
造成珊瑚礁消失的最後一個因素是人類。人們有時會駕船撞上珊瑚礁，或在上面拋錨，折斷大塊的珊瑚。在珊瑚礁上行走的潛水者也可能造成嚴重的破壞。此外，有些人甚至因為珊瑚色彩繽紛又漂亮，而把它折下來當作紀念品收藏。
我們要如何幫助珊瑚礁？我們需要多瞭解它們，並共同努力阻止可能威脅其生存的活動。
title: 珊瑚礁的危機

text: Aesop, the Greek writer of fables, was sitting by the roadside one day when a traveler asked him what sort of people lived in Athens. Aesop replied, “Tell me where you come from and what sort of people live there, and I’ll tell you what sort of people you’ll find in Athens.” {{16}}, the man answered, “I come from Argos, and there the people are all friendly, generous, and warm-hearted. I love them.”
{{17}} this, Aesop answered, “I’m happy to tell you, my dear friend, that you’ll find the people of Athens much the same.”

A few hours later, {{18}} traveler came down the road. He too stopped and asked Aesop the same question. {{19}}, Aesop made the same request. But frowning, the man answered, “I’m from Argos and there the people are unfriendly, {{20}}, and vicious. They’re thieves and murderers, all of them.” “Well, I’m afraid you’ll find the people of Athens much the same,” replied Aesop.

qs.ex: 空格為分詞構句，表示旅人回答時的神情，後文第二位旅人 frowning（皺眉）與之對比，故選 Smiling。
At this 表示「聽到這番話時」，at 引導對某事的反應，故選 At。
traveler 為單數可數名詞，且前文已有一位旅人，a few hours later 來了「另一位」，用 another traveler。
第二位旅人問同樣的問題，伊索「再次」提出同樣的要求，用 Again。
與 unfriendly、vicious 並列的負面形容詞，mean（刻薄的）最合。

zh: 寫寓言的希臘作家伊索有一天坐在路邊，這時一位旅人問他雅典住著什麼樣的人。伊索回答：「告訴我你來自哪裡、那裡住著什麼樣的人，我就告訴你在雅典會遇到什麼樣的人。」那人微笑著回答：「我來自阿爾戈斯，那裡的人都友善、慷慨又熱心，我愛他們。」
聽了這番話，伊索回答：「親愛的朋友，我很高興地告訴你，你會發現雅典的人也差不多是這樣。」
幾個小時後，另一位旅人沿著路走來。他也停下來，向伊索問了同樣的問題。伊索再次提出同樣的要求。但那人皺著眉頭回答：「我來自阿爾戈斯，那裡的人不友善、刻薄又惡毒。他們全都是小偷和殺人犯。」伊索回答：「嗯，恐怕你會發現雅典的人也差不多是這樣。」
title: 伊索寓言：雅典人是怎樣的人

text: Every year tens of thousands of tourists visit Mount Kilimanjaro, the highest mountain in Tanzania, Africa, to witness the scenes depicted in Earnest Hemingway’s The Snows of Kilimanjaro. They are attracted by the American writer’s {{21}} of the millennia-old glaciers. However, this tourist attraction will soon {{22}}. According to the Climate Change Group, formed by environmentalists worldwide to document the effects of global warming, Mount Kilimanjaro’s snows and glaciers are melting and are {{23}} to disappear by 2020. Not only will the summit lose its tourist attraction, but the disappearance of the snows will also cause major damage to the ecosystem on the dry African plains at its base. {{24}} the snow covering the peak, there will not be enough moisture and water to nourish the plants and animals below. Rising temperatures, an effect of global warming, {{25}} threaten the ecosystem of this mountain area. The loss of snows on the 5,892m peak, which have been there for about 11,700 years, could have disastrous effects on Tanzania.

qs.ex: 遊客被作家對千年冰河的 descriptions（描寫）所吸引，與前面 scenes depicted 呼應。
後文說冰雪將消融，故此景點即將 vanish（消失）。
be likely to disappear（很可能消失）；capable 須接 of + V-ing，不接 to V，ready 語意不合。
Without the snow covering the peak（沒有覆蓋山頂的積雪），後句說水分不足，故用 Without。
thus 表示結果：氣溫上升因而也威脅生態系，副詞連接前後句。

zh: 每年有數以萬計的遊客造訪非洲坦尚尼亞的最高峰吉力馬札羅山，想親眼見到海明威《吉力馬札羅的雪》中所描寫的景象。他們被這位美國作家對千年冰河的描寫所吸引。然而，這個觀光景點很快就會消失。全球環保人士為記錄全球暖化影響而成立的氣候變遷小組指出，吉力馬札羅山的積雪與冰河正在融化，很可能在 2020 年前消失。山頂不但會失去觀光魅力，積雪消失也會對山腳乾燥的非洲平原生態系統造成重大破壞。少了覆蓋山頂的積雪，就沒有足夠的水氣與水分來滋養山下的動植物。氣溫上升是全球暖化的影響之一，也因此威脅這個山區的生態系統。這座海拔 5,892 公尺的山峰上已存在約 11,700 年的積雪一旦消失，可能對坦尚尼亞造成災難性的後果。
title: 吉力馬札羅山的雪

text: Most human beings actually decide before they think. When people encounter a complex issue and form an opinion, how thoroughly have they {{26}} all the important factors involved before they make their decisions? The answer is: not very thoroughly, {{27}} they are executives, specialized experts, or ordinary people in the street. Very few people, no matter how intelligent or experienced, can {{28}} all the possibilities or outcomes of a policy or a course of action within just a short period of time. Those who take pride in being decisive often try their best to consider all the factors beforehand. {{29}}, it is not unusual for them to come up with a decision before they have the time to do so. And {{30}} an opinion is formed, most of their thinking then is simply trying to find support for it.

qs.ex: have examined all the important factors（仔細檢視各項因素），過去分詞，examine 符合 thoroughly。
whether they are A, B, or C 表示「無論是…還是…」，whether 引導讓步子句。
短時間內難以 take into account（考慮）所有可能與結果，固定片語。
前句說盡力事先考慮，後句說卻常先下決定，轉折，用 However。
once an opinion is formed（一旦形成意見），once 引導時間副詞子句。

zh: 大多數人其實是先做決定、後思考。人們遇到複雜的議題並形成看法時，在做出決定之前，究竟多徹底地檢視了所有相關的重要因素？答案是：不太徹底，不論是主管、專家或街上的一般人都一樣。無論多聰明或多有經驗，很少有人能在短短的時間內把一項政策或一個行動方案的所有可能性或結果都納入考慮。那些以果斷自豪的人常常盡力事先考慮所有因素。然而，他們還來不及這麼做就已做出決定，這種情形並不罕見。而且一旦形成了意見，他們之後大部分的思考，只是在設法為它尋找支持。
title: 人先決定再思考

text: In English-speaking cultures, the choice of first names for children can be prompted by many factors: tradition, religion, nature, culture, and fashion, to name just a few.

Certain people like to give a name that has been handed down in the family to show {{31}} for or to remember a relative whom they love or admire. Some families have a tradition of {{32}} the father’s first name to the first born son. In other families, a surname is included in the selection of a child’s given name to {{33}} a family surname going. It may be the mother’s maiden name, for instance.

For a long time, {{34}} has also played an important role in naming children. Boys’ names such as John, Peter, and Thomas are chosen from the Bible. Girls’ names such as Faith, Patience, and Sophie (wisdom) are chosen because they symbolize Christian qualities. However, for people who are not necessarily religious but are fond of nature, names {{35}} things of beauty are often favored. Flower and plant names like Heather, Rosemary, and Iris {{36}} this category.

Another factor that has had a great {{37}} on the choice of names is the spread of culture through the media. People may choose a name because they are strongly {{38}} a character in a book or a television series; they may also adopt names of famous people or their favorite actors and actresses. Sometimes, people pick foreign names for their children because those names are unusual and will thus make their children more {{39}} and distinctive.

Finally, some people just pick a name the sound of which they like, {{40}} of its meaning, its origins, or its popularity. However, even these people may look at the calendar to pick a lucky day when they make their choice.

qs.ex: show respect for（表示敬意），與 remember 並列，需名詞 respect。
a tradition of 後接動名詞，passing down the father’s first name（把父親的名字傳給長子）。
to 後接原形動詞，keep a family surname going（讓家族姓氏延續下去）。
後文談聖經與基督教特質，主詞需名詞，故為 religion。
names involving things of beauty（涉及美麗事物的名字），現在分詞後置修飾 names。
主詞 Flower and plant names 為複數，用不加 -s 的現在式 fall into，fall into this category 意為「屬於這個類別」。
a great impact on（對…有很大影響），名詞。
be strongly drawn to（深受…吸引），過去分詞加 to。
與 distinctive 並列的形容詞，使孩子更 unique（獨特）。
regardless of（不顧、不論），與後面 of 搭配。

zh: 在說英語的文化中，為孩子選擇名字的原因可能有很多，傳統、宗教、自然、文化與流行只是其中幾項。
有些人喜歡取一個在家族中代代相傳的名字，以表達對所愛或敬佩的親人的敬意，或紀念他們。有些家庭有把父親的名字傳給長子的傳統。在其他家庭中，孩子的名字裡會包含一個姓氏，好讓家族的姓氏延續下去，例如可能是母親的娘家姓。
長久以來，宗教也在為孩子命名上扮演重要角色。John、Peter、Thomas 等男孩的名字取自聖經。Faith、Patience、Sophie（智慧）等女孩的名字，是因為象徵基督教的美德而被選用。然而，對於不一定信教但喜愛大自然的人來說，與美麗事物有關的名字常受青睞。Heather、Rosemary、Iris 等花草的名字就屬於這一類。
另一個對取名有很大影響的因素是媒體所帶來的文化傳播。人們可能因為深受書籍或電視影集中某個角色的吸引而選擇某個名字；他們也可能採用名人或自己喜愛的演員的名字。有時人們為孩子取外國名字，因為這些名字不常見，因此會讓孩子更獨特、與眾不同。
最後，有些人挑名字只看自己喜不喜歡它的發音，而不管它的意義、起源或受歡迎程度。不過，即使是這些人，在做決定時也可能會看日曆挑個吉日。
title: 英語文化中為孩子取名

text: Tai Chi Chuan is a type of ancient Chinese martial art. People {{16}} Tai Chi mainly for its health benefits. This centuries-old Chinese mind-body exercise is now gaining popularity in the United States.

The most familiar aspect of Tai Chi Chuan is the hand form, which is a series of slow-flowing movements with poetic names {{17}} “dragons stirring up the wind” and “wave hands like clouds.” These movements, forming an exercise system, {{18}} one to effortlessly experience the vital life force, or the Qi energy, in one’s body.

Tai Chi Chuan is not only a physical but also a {{19}} exercise. Psychologically, this exercise may increase communication between the body and the mind and enable one to deal with other people more effectively. It {{20}} stress and creates calmness and confidence. Relaxation and a feeling of joy are among the first noticeable differences in a Tai Chi student.

qs.ex: practice Tai Chi（練習太極拳），主詞 People 為複數，現在式動詞不加 -s。
poetic names like “dragons stirring up the wind”（像…這樣的詩意名稱），like 引出例子。
These movements 為複數主詞，forming an exercise system 為修飾語，主要動詞用複數 allow（allow one to …，讓人能…）。
not only physical but also mental exercise（不只是身體，也是心理的運動），與後文 Psychologically 呼應。
同一句後半說 creates calmness and confidence（帶來平靜與自信），前半應與之呼應，故為 reduces stress（減輕壓力）。

zh: 太極拳是一種古老的中國武術。人們練習太極拳主要是為了它對健康的益處。這種已有數百年歷史的中國身心運動，現在在美國越來越受歡迎。
太極拳最為人熟悉的部分是徒手套路，也就是一連串緩慢流暢的動作，並有詩意的名稱，例如「龍攪風」與「雲手」。這些動作形成一套運動體系，讓人毫不費力地體驗身體裡的生命力，也就是氣的能量。
太極拳不僅是身體的運動，也是心理的運動。就心理而言，這項運動可以增進身體與心靈之間的溝通，並使人更有效地與他人相處。它能減輕壓力，帶來平靜與自信。放鬆與喜悅的感覺，是太極學員身上最先可察覺的改變之一。
title: 太極拳

text: Much like the dove and robin, the bluebird is considered a very lucky sign in most cultures, particularly when seen in the spring. {{21}}, a woodpecker, when seen near the home, is regarded as a good sign. In contrast, the peacock is not {{22}} seen as lucky. In places like India, the peacock is considered lucky because the great many “eyes” on its feathers are said to alert it to {{23}} evil. Peacocks are also highly valued in China and Japan, where they are kept as symbols by the ruling families to {{24}} their status and wealth. However, the peacock receives only scorn from the rest of the world. The feathers of peacocks are considered the most {{25}} part of the bird because the eye-shaped markings on them are associated with “evil eyes.” To bring the evil eye into the home is thus believed to invite trouble and sorrow.

qs.ex: 前句說藍鳥是吉兆，本句說啄木鳥也被視為吉兆，語意相似，用 Similarly。
In contrast 後說孔雀並非 universally（普遍地）被視為幸運，與 In places like India 呼應。
alert it to approaching evil（警示牠有逼近的邪惡），現在分詞作形容詞修飾 evil。
家族把孔雀當作象徵，用來代表（represent）其地位與財富。
孔雀羽毛上有「邪惡之眼」的圖案，故被視為最不吉利（unlucky）的部分。

zh: 就像鴿子與知更鳥一樣，藍鳥在大多數文化中被視為非常幸運的徵兆，尤其是在春天看見時。同樣地，啄木鳥出現在家附近時，也被視為好兆頭。相對地，孔雀並非普遍被視為幸運。在印度等地，孔雀被認為是幸運的，因為牠羽毛上的許多「眼睛」據說能讓牠警覺到逼近的邪惡。孔雀在中國與日本也備受珍視，統治家族把牠們當作象徵來飼養，代表自己的地位與財富。然而在世界其他地方，孔雀卻只受到輕視。孔雀的羽毛被視為這種鳥最不吉利的部分，因為羽毛上眼睛形狀的斑紋會讓人聯想到「邪眼」。因此，據信把邪眼帶進家中，會招來麻煩與悲傷。
title: 孔雀是幸運還是不幸？

text: Nutritional products that can be collected from trees include fruits, nuts, seeds, leaves, and bark. Tree products have been an important part of diets for thousands of years, from early humans {{26}} fruits and nuts to the first cultivation of important trees, such as mango and apple.

The apple is one of the world’s most cultivated fruit trees, {{27}} over 7,000 different kinds in existence. Despite their great {{28}}, however, most domesticated apples can be traced back to a common ancestor, the wild apple of Central Asia, Malus sieversii. Apples have been grown for thousands of years in Asia and Europe, and {{29}} to North America by European colonists in the 17th century. Today, apples are {{30}} eaten the world over and form the basis for multi-million dollar industries. In 2005, at least 55 million tons of apples were grown worldwide, which generated a value of about $10 billion.

qs.ex: early humans gathering fruits and nuts，現在分詞後置修飾 humans，表示「採集…的早期人類」。
with over 7,000 different kinds in existence 為 with 引導的附帶狀況，說明品種超過七千種。
後面 Despite their great variety（儘管品種繁多），但多數可追溯至共同祖先，語意對比。
主詞 Apples 與 bring 為被動關係（由 European colonists 帶來），過去時間 in the 17th century，用 were brought。
apples are regularly eaten the world over（全世界經常食用），regularly 符合語意。

zh: 可以從樹上採集的營養產品包括水果、堅果、種子、葉子與樹皮。樹木產品數千年來一直是飲食中重要的一環，從早期人類採集水果與堅果，到最早栽培芒果與蘋果等重要樹種。
蘋果是世界上最廣泛栽培的果樹之一，現存的品種超過 7,000 種。然而，儘管品種繁多，大多數馴化的蘋果都可追溯到共同的祖先，也就是中亞的野生蘋果 Malus sieversii。蘋果在亞洲與歐洲已栽種數千年，並在 17 世紀由歐洲殖民者帶到北美。如今，全世界的人經常食用蘋果，蘋果也成為數百萬美元產業的基礎。2005 年，全世界的蘋果產量至少有 5,500 萬噸，創造出約 100 億美元的價值。
title: 蘋果與樹木的營養產品

text: A paperclip, made of steel wire bent into a hooped shape, is an instrument used to hold sheets of paper together. This common {{31}} is a wonder of simplicity and function. But where did this simple, cheap, and indispensable invention come from?

In the late 19th century, the most common way to hold papers together was by using a pin. Although the pin was an inexpensive tool and was easily {{32}}, it would leave holes in the paper. Later, as steel wire became more common, inventors began to notice its elastic feature. With this feature, it could be stretched and {{33}} various clip-like objects. In the years just prior to 1900, quite a few paperclip designs emerged. The name most frequently {{34}} the paperclip invention is Johan Vaaler, a Norwegian inventor. However, Vaaler’s clips were not the same as the paperclips currently in use. Specifically, they did not have the interior loop we see today. The {{35}} looped design was invented by Gem Manufacturing Ltd. in England. This clip is therefore sometimes {{36}} the Gem clip.

Because of Vaaler, the paperclip played an important {{37}} role in Norway. During World War II, Norway was occupied by the Nazis. Norwegians were prohibited from wearing any {{38}} of their national unity, such as buttons with the initials of their king. Thus, in {{39}}, they started wearing paperclips to show their solidarity. The reason for doing this was simple: Paperclips were a Norwegian invention whose original function was to bind together. After the war, a giant paperclip statue was erected in Oslo to {{40}} Vaaler—even though his design was never actually manufactured.

qs.ex: This common device（這個常見的器具），名詞，呼應前面的 instrument。
was easily removable（容易被取下），形容詞，與 inexpensive 並列。
could be stretched and twisted into various clip-like objects（被扭成各種夾子狀物品），過去分詞片語。
the name most frequently associated with the invention（最常與這項發明聯想在一起的名字），過去分詞後置修飾。
The familiar looped design（人們熟悉的迴圈設計），形容詞，與 Vaaler 沒有迴圈的設計相對比。
sometimes known as the Gem clip（有時被稱為 Gem 夾），be known as 固定用法。
played an important historical role（扮演重要的歷史角色），形容詞修飾 role。
wearing any symbol of their national unity（任何代表國家團結的象徵），名詞。
in protest（作為抗議），in 後接名詞。
to honor Vaaler（向 Vaaler 致敬），to 後接原形動詞。

zh: 迴紋針是由鋼絲彎成環形做成的，是用來把紙張夾在一起的器具。這種常見的器具既簡單又實用，堪稱奇蹟。但這個簡單、便宜又不可或缺的發明是從哪裡來的呢？

19 世紀晚期，把紙張固定在一起最常見的方法是用別針。別針雖然便宜，也容易取下，卻會在紙上留下小洞。後來，隨著鋼絲變得更普遍，發明家開始注意到它的彈性。憑著這項特性，鋼絲可以被拉長、扭成各種夾子狀的物品。在 1900 年前不久，出現了不少迴紋針的設計。最常與迴紋針發明聯想在一起的名字是挪威發明家約翰·瓦勒。然而，瓦勒的迴紋針與目前使用的並不相同。具體來說，它們沒有我們今天看到的內圈。我們熟悉的迴圈設計是英國的 Gem 製造公司發明的，因此這種迴紋針有時被稱為 Gem 夾。
因為瓦勒，迴紋針在挪威扮演了重要的歷史角色。第二次世界大戰期間，挪威被納粹占領。挪威人被禁止配戴任何象徵國家團結的東西，例如印有國王姓名縮寫的鈕扣。於是，他們開始配戴迴紋針表示抗議，並藉此展現團結。原因很簡單：迴紋針是挪威人的發明，其原本的功能就是把東西綁在一起。戰後，奧斯陸豎立了一座巨大的迴紋針雕像來向瓦勒致敬，儘管他的設計其實從未真正生產過。
title: 迴紋針的由來

text: Bill and Sam decided to kidnap the son of a banker to compensate for their business loss. They kidnapped the boy and hid him in a cave. They asked for a ransom of $2,000 to return the boy. {{16}}, their plan quickly got out of control. Their young captive {{17}} to be a mischievous boy. He viewed the kidnapping as a wonderful camping trip. He demanded that his kidnappers play tiring games with him, such as riding Bill as a horse for nine miles. Bill and Sam were soon desperate and decided to {{18}} the little terror. They lowered the price to $1,500. Yet, knowing perfectly well {{19}} a troublemaker his son was, the father refused to give them any money. {{20}}, he asked the kidnappers to pay him $250 to take the boy back. To persuade the boy to return home, Bill and Sam had to tell him that his father was taking him bear-hunting. The kidnappers finally handed over the boy and $250 to the banker and fled town as quickly as they could.

qs.ex: 前句要贖金、後句計畫失控，語意轉折，用 However。
turn out to be 意為「結果是」，表示男孩原來是個頑皮鬼。
兩人已絕望，想擺脫這個小魔頭，get rid of 意為「擺脫」。
what a troublemaker his son was 為感嘆句結構，what + a + 名詞，故選 what。
父親不但不付錢，反而要綁匪付錢，Instead 表示「反而」。

zh: 比爾與山姆決定綁架一位銀行家的兒子，以彌補生意上的虧損。他們綁走男孩，把他藏在山洞裡，並索取兩千美元的贖金才肯放人。然而，他們的計畫很快就失控了。這個年幼的人質原來是個調皮搗蛋的男孩，他把綁架當成一場精彩的露營之旅，還要求綁匪陪他玩累人的遊戲，例如把比爾當馬騎，一騎就是九英里。比爾和山姆很快就絕望了，決定擺脫這個小惡魔。他們把價碼降到一千五百美元。然而，父親非常清楚自己的兒子是多麼愛惹麻煩，拒絕給他們半毛錢。他反而要綁匪付他兩百五十美元才肯把男孩帶回去。為了說服男孩回家，比爾和山姆只好告訴他，他爸爸要帶他去獵熊。綁匪終於把男孩和兩百五十美元交給銀行家，然後盡快逃離了小鎮。
title: 綁架頑皮少年

text: A polygraph machine, also known as a “lie detector,” is a common part of criminal investigations. The instrument is used to measure {{21}} a person’s body reacts to questions. The theory underlying it is that lying is stressful, and that this stress can be measured and recorded on a polygraph machine.

When a person takes a polygraph test, four to six wires, called sensors, are {{22}} to different parts of his body. The sensors pick up signals from the person’s blood pressure, pulse, and perspiration. {{23}} the process of questioning, all the signals are recorded on a single strip of moving paper. Once the questions are finished, the examiner analyzes the results to determine if the person tested {{24}} truthful.

Well-trained examiners can usually detect lying with a high degree of {{25}} when they use a polygraph. However, because different people behave differently when lying, a polygraph test is by no means perfect.

qs.ex: measure how a person’s body reacts 表示「測量身體如何反應」，名詞子句用 how。
感測線要「連接／貼附」在身體各部位，be attached to 為固定搭配。
訊號是在整個詢問過程中被記錄，Throughout the process 意為「在整個過程中」。
if the person tested was being truthful，表示受測當下是否說實話，用過去進行式。
a high degree of accuracy 意為「高準確度」，與後句「並非完美」呼應。

zh: 多項生理記錄儀又稱「測謊機」，是刑事調查中常見的工具。這種儀器用來測量一個人的身體對提問如何反應。其背後的理論是：說謊會造成壓力，而這種壓力可以由測謊機測量並記錄下來。
人在接受測謊時，會有四到六條稱為感測器的線連接到身體的不同部位。這些感測器會接收來自此人血壓、脈搏與排汗的訊號。在整個詢問過程中，所有訊號都被記錄在一條移動的紙帶上。問題問完之後，檢測人員會分析結果，以判定受測者是否誠實。
訓練有素的檢測人員使用測謊機時，通常能以很高的準確度偵測出謊言。然而，由於不同的人說謊時的表現不同，測謊絕對稱不上完美。
title: 測謊機運作原理

text: International trade is the exchange of goods and services between countries. Trade is driven by different production costs in different countries, making {{26}} cheaper for some countries to import goods rather than make them. A country is said to have a comparative advantage over another when it can produce a commodity more cheaply. This comparative advantage is {{27}} by key factors of production such as land, capital, and labor.

While international trade has long been conducted in history, its economic, social, and political importance has been {{28}} in recent centuries. During the 1990s, international trade grew by nearly 8.6% each year. In the year 1990 alone, the growth in trade in services was as high as 19%.

Today, all countries are involved in, and to varying degrees dependent on, trade with other countries. {{29}} international trade, nations would be limited to the goods and services produced within their own borders. Trade is certainly a main {{30}} force for globalization. It is also the subject of many international agreements that aim to govern and facilitate international trade, such as those negotiated through the World Trade Organization (WTO).

qs.ex: making it cheaper to import... 中 it 為形式受詞，真受詞是後面的不定詞片語。
比較利益是由土地、資本、勞力等關鍵生產要素所「決定」，be determined by。
重要性在近幾世紀「日益提升」，on the rise 意為「上升中」。
沒有國際貿易，各國就只能用自己境內的產品，Without 引導假設語氣。
a main driving force 意為「主要推動力」，修飾 force 用現在分詞。

zh: 國際貿易是國與國之間商品與服務的交換。貿易的推動力來自各國不同的生產成本，使得某些國家進口商品比自己製造更便宜。當一個國家生產某項商品的成本比另一國低時，就稱該國對另一國具有比較利益。這種比較利益是由土地、資本和勞力等關鍵生產要素所決定的。
雖然國際貿易在歷史上由來已久，但其經濟、社會與政治上的重要性在近幾個世紀日益提升。1990 年代，國際貿易每年成長近 8.6%。光是 1990 年一年，服務貿易的成長率就高達 19%。
如今，所有國家都與其他國家進行貿易，並在不同程度上依賴貿易。沒有國際貿易，各國就只能使用境內所生產的商品與服務。貿易無疑是全球化的主要推動力，也是許多國際協定的主題，這些協定旨在規範並促進國際貿易，例如透過世界貿易組織（WTO）所談判達成的協定。
title: 國際貿易

text: Are forests always created by nature? A man from rural India proves that this is not necessarily {{31}}.

Abdul Kareem, who used to be an airline ticketing agent, has a great love for the woods. Though he never went to college, he can talk about plants and trees like an expert. In 1977, he bought a piece of rocky wasteland with the {{32}} of growing trees on it. In the beginning, people thought he was {{33}} to waste his time and money on the land. But he simply {{34}} them and kept working on the soil and planting trees there. The land was so {{35}} that it had to be watered several times a day. Kareem had to fetch the water from a source that was a kilometer away. In the first two years, none of the trees he planted {{36}}. However, in the third year, several young trees started growing. Greatly {{37}} by the result, Kareem planted more trees and his man-made forest began to take shape.

Kareem let his forest grow naturally, without using fertilizers or insecticides. He believed in the ability of nature to renew itself without the {{38}} of humans. That’s why he did not allow fallen leaves or twigs from the forest to be removed.

After years of hard work, Kareem has not only realized his dream but also transformed a piece of {{39}} property into a beautiful forest. Today, his forest is home to 1,500 medicinal plants, 2,000 varieties of trees, rare birds, animals, and insects. Now, scientists from all over the world come to visit his {{40}}. They hope to find the secret of his success.

qs.ex: 空格是 is 的補語（necessarily 為副詞），此處填形容詞，this is not necessarily true 意為「未必如此」。
with the vision of growing trees，名詞，指「願景」，表示買地的目的。
was crazy to waste... 形容詞，人們認為他瘋了才浪費錢。
but 表轉折，過去式動詞 ignored 意為「不理會」那些人。
形容詞 dry，土地太乾燥，所以一天得澆好幾次水。
none of the trees survived 動詞，前兩年沒有一棵樹存活。
Greatly encouraged by the result，過去分詞，受到結果鼓舞。
名詞 interference，without the interference of humans 意為「沒有人為干預」。
形容詞 deserted，荒廢的土地，與 rocky wasteland 呼應。
名詞 creation，指他的作品，即人造森林。

zh: 森林一定是由大自然造就的嗎？一位來自印度鄉間的男子證明，這未必如此。

阿卜杜勒．卡里姆曾是航空公司的售票員，對樹林懷有深深的熱愛。雖然他從未上過大學，卻能像專家一樣談論植物與樹木。1977 年，他買下一片多石的荒地，懷著在那裡種樹的願景。起初，人們認為他瘋了才會把時間與金錢浪費在那片土地上。但他完全不理會他們，持續整理土壤並在那裡種樹。那片土地太乾燥，一天得澆好幾次水。卡里姆必須從一公里外的水源取水。頭兩年，他種下的樹沒有一棵存活。然而，到了第三年，幾棵幼樹開始生長。這個結果讓卡里姆大受鼓舞，於是種了更多樹，他的人造森林也開始成形。
卡里姆讓他的森林自然生長，不使用肥料或殺蟲劑。他相信大自然有自我更新的能力，無須人類干預。這就是為什麼他不准人把森林裡掉落的葉子或細枝移走。
經過多年的辛勤付出，卡里姆不僅實現了夢想，還把一塊荒廢的土地變成了美麗的森林。如今，他的森林是 1,500 種藥用植物、2,000 種樹木，以及珍稀鳥類、動物和昆蟲的家園。現在，世界各地的科學家都來參觀他的作品，希望找出他成功的祕訣。
title: 印度男子打造人造森林

text: You begin to notice a bit of pain on your eyelid each time you blink. You {{16}} the mirror to find a tiny red spot on the base of your lower lashes. These {{17}} are probably the beginning of an eye stye. An eye stye is a small bump, resembling a pimple, that develops when an oil gland at the edge of an eyelid becomes infected by bacteria. These bacteria are found in the nose and are easily {{18}} to the eye when you rub your nose, then your eye. Pus will build up in the center of the stye, causing a yellowish spot. Usually a stye is accompanied by a swollen eye.

{{19}} a stye can look unpleasant at times, it is usually harmless and doesn’t cause vision problems. Most styes heal on their own within a few days. You might speed up healing time by gently pressing a warm washcloth {{20}} your eyelid for 10 minutes, 3 or 4 times a day. Make sure you don’t squeeze or pop a stye like you would a pimple. Doing so may cause a severe eye infection.

qs.ex: look into the mirror 意為「照鏡子、往鏡中看」，look into 可接鏡子。
眼瞼疼痛與紅點是麥粒腫的「症狀」。
細菌從鼻子被「轉移」到眼睛，be transferred to。
前後語意轉折（看起來不舒服，但無害），用 Although。
把溫熱毛巾壓在眼瞼上，press ... against 意為「壓靠在」。

zh: 你開始注意到每次眨眼時眼瞼有點痛。你照鏡子，發現下睫毛根部有一個小紅點。這些症狀很可能是麥粒腫（針眼）的開端。麥粒腫是一種類似青春痘的小腫塊，當眼瞼邊緣的油脂腺被細菌感染時就會形成。這些細菌存在於鼻子裡，當你先揉鼻子再揉眼睛時，就很容易被轉移到眼睛。膿會在麥粒腫中央累積，形成淡黃色的斑點。麥粒腫通常伴隨眼睛腫脹。
雖然麥粒腫有時看起來令人不舒服，但通常無害，也不會造成視力問題。大多數麥粒腫會在幾天內自行痊癒。你可以每天 3、4 次，將溫熱的毛巾輕輕壓在眼瞼上 10 分鐘，以加速癒合。千萬不要像擠青春痘那樣擠壓或戳破麥粒腫，這樣做可能會造成嚴重的眼睛感染。
title: 麥粒腫（針眼）

text: Shoes are hugely important for protecting our feet, especially in places like Africa, where healthcare provision is limited. Unfortunately, shoes are not always readily available for people living in poverty, {{21}} shoes that are the right size. Almost as soon as a child receives shoes to wear, he/she is likely to have grown out of them. Then the child has to {{22}} with shoes that are too small. The Shoe That Grows, created by a charity called Because International, changes all this. It allows children to {{23}} their shoes’ size as their feet grow.

The innovative footwear resembles a common sandal and is made of leather straps and rubber soles, a material similar to that used in tires. They come {{24}} two sizes, and can expand in three places. The straps on the heel and toe control the length of the shoe, {{25}} the two on either side allow for different widths. With this special design, the shoes can “grow” up to five sizes and last for at least five years.

qs.ex: 貧窮的人連鞋子都不一定有，更別說合腳的鞋，let alone 意為「更不用說」。
make do with 意為「將就使用」，孩子只能將就穿太小的鞋。
隨腳長大「調整」鞋子尺寸。
come in two sizes 意為「有兩種尺寸」。
前者控制長度，while 引導對比，後者控制寬度。

zh: 鞋子對保護我們的雙腳極為重要，尤其是在非洲這類醫療服務有限的地方。不幸的是，生活貧困的人不一定能輕易取得鞋子，更不用說合腳的鞋了。孩子幾乎一拿到鞋子，腳就很可能已經長大，穿不下了。接著孩子只好將就穿太小的鞋。由名為 Because International 的慈善機構所設計的「會長大的鞋子」改變了這一切。它讓孩子能隨著腳長大而調整鞋子的尺寸。
這種創新的鞋款外形像一般涼鞋，由皮革帶與橡膠鞋底製成，鞋底材質與輪胎所用的類似。鞋子有兩種尺寸，並可在三處擴展。腳跟與腳趾處的帶子控制鞋長，而兩側的兩條帶子則可調整鞋寬。有了這種特殊設計，鞋子可以「長大」多達五個尺碼，且至少能穿五年。
title: 會長大的鞋子

text: Research has proven that weather plays a part in our moods: Warmer temperatures and exposure to sunshine increase positive thinking, whereas cold, rainy days bring anxiety and fatigue. {{26}}, many people believe that bad weather can reduce productivity and efficiency.

There is, however, a significant {{27}} between such beliefs and the actual effect of weather on people’s performance at work. Using empirical data from laboratory experiments {{28}} observations of a mid-sized Japanese bank in real life, researchers find that weather conditions indeed influence a worker’s focus. When the weather is bad, individuals tend to focus more on their work rather than thinking about activities they could {{29}} outside of work. But photos showing outdoor activities, such as sailing on a sunny day or walking in the woods, can greatly distract workers and thus {{30}} their productivity. The findings conclude that workers are actually most productive when the weather is lousy—and only if nothing reminds them of good weather.

qs.ex: 天氣影響心情，因此（Accordingly）許多人相信壞天氣會降低效率，為因果關係。
前句說信念，後句 however 指出信念與實際影響之間有「落差」。
實驗資料「以及」真實觀察，as well as 表並列。
工作之外可以「從事」的活動，engage in。
照片讓人分心，因而「降低」生產力。

zh: 研究已證實，天氣對我們的情緒有影響：較高的氣溫和日照會增加正面思考，而寒冷多雨的日子則帶來焦慮與疲倦。因此，許多人相信壞天氣會降低生產力與效率。

然而，這類信念與天氣對工作表現的實際影響之間存在著顯著落差。研究人員利用實驗室實驗的實證資料，以及對一家日本中型銀行的實地觀察發現，天氣狀況確實會影響員工的專注力。天氣不好時，人們傾向更專注於工作，而不是去想工作之外可以從事的活動。但展示戶外活動的照片，例如在晴天駕帆船或在林中散步，會讓員工嚴重分心，進而降低他們的生產力。研究結論是：員工其實在天氣糟糕時最有生產力，但前提是沒有任何東西讓他們想起好天氣。
title: 天氣與工作效率

text: The widespread popularity of onions is not limited to modern-day kitchens. There is evidence of onions being used for culinary and medicinal purposes all over the ancient world. Nonetheless, no culture {{31}} onions quite as much as the ancient Egyptians. For them, the onion was not just food or medicine; it held significant {{32}} meaning. Onions were considered to be {{33}} of eternal life. The circle-within-a-circle structure of an onion, for them, {{34}} the eternity of existence. According to certain documents, ancient Egyptians also used onions for medicinal purposes, but they likely would have viewed the {{35}} power of the vegetable as magical, rather than medical.

Onions are depicted in many paintings {{36}} inside pyramids and tombs that span the history of ancient Egypt. They {{37}} as a funeral offering shown upon the altars of the gods. The dead were buried with onions and onion flowers on or around various {{38}} of their bodies. Mummies have also been found with onions and onion flowers {{39}} their pelvis, chest, ears, eyes, and feet.

Some scholars theorize that onions may have been used for the dead because it was believed that their strong scent would {{40}} the dead to breathe again. Other researchers believe it was because onions were known for their special curative properties, which would be helpful in the afterlife.

qs.ex: 動詞過去式 admired，no culture admired onions quite as much as the ancient Egyptians 意為「沒有任何文化像古埃及人那樣推崇洋蔥」。
形容詞 spiritual 修飾 meaning，洋蔥具有「精神／宗教」上的意義。
名詞複數 symbols，be considered to be symbols of eternal life。
動詞過去式 reflected，圓中有圓的結構「反映」永恆的存在。
形容詞 healing，the healing power 意為「療癒力」。
過去分詞 discovered，paintings discovered inside pyramids 意為「在金字塔內發現的畫」。
動詞 functioned，function as 意為「作為……」，洋蔥作為祭品。
名詞複數 parts，various parts of their bodies 意為「身體各部位」。
現在分詞 decorating，洋蔥花「裝飾」骨盆、胸部等處。
動詞原形 prompt，would prompt the dead to breathe again，促使死者再次呼吸。

zh: 洋蔥廣受喜愛，並不只限於現代的廚房。有證據顯示，在整個古代世界，洋蔥都被用於烹飪與醫療用途。儘管如此，沒有任何文化像古埃及人那樣推崇洋蔥。對他們而言，洋蔥不只是食物或藥物，它還具有重大的精神意義。洋蔥被視為永生的象徵。對他們來說，洋蔥圓中有圓的結構反映了存在的永恆。根據某些文獻，古埃及人也將洋蔥用於醫療，但他們很可能把這種蔬菜的療癒力視為一種魔力，而不是醫學上的療效。
洋蔥出現在許多在金字塔與墓室內發現的畫作中，這些畫作橫跨古埃及的整個歷史。畫中的洋蔥是喪葬祭品，供奉在眾神的祭壇上。死者下葬時，身體的各個部位上或周圍都放有洋蔥和洋蔥花。人們也發現木乃伊的骨盆、胸部、耳朵、眼睛和腳上都裝飾著洋蔥和洋蔥花。
一些學者推測，洋蔥之所以用在死者身上，可能是因為人們相信洋蔥強烈的氣味能促使死者再次呼吸。其他研究者則認為，是因為洋蔥以其特殊的療效而聞名，這在來世會有幫助。
title: 古埃及人與洋蔥

text: It has long been assumed that creativity is some unusual trait enjoyed by the few. However, according to a wide array of scientific and sociological research, creativity is {{16}} a sign of rare genius than a natural human potential. Thus, it can be nurtured and encouraged.

It is believed that taking breaks from a problem can help {{17}} a moment of insight or stimulate new ideas. Unconventional solutions can also be explored. That is why some of the most successful companies in the world, such as 3M and Google, encourage their employees to {{18}} all sorts of relaxing activities, such as playing pinball and wandering about the campus. During such breaks, the mind turns inward, {{19}} it can subconsciously puzzle over subtle meanings and connections.

Another way to increase creativity is to take risks. This is because many breakthroughs come up when people venture {{20}} their usual routines or areas of expertise. This can be done by, for example, learning new skills or traveling to new countries.

qs.ex: less a sign of rare genius than a natural potential，less ... than 意為「與其說是……不如說是」。
spark a moment of insight 意為「激發靈光一閃」。
員工參與放鬆活動，take part in 意為「參與」。
where 前有逗號，為關係副詞的非限定用法（= and there），指心智轉向的內在，在那裡可於潛意識中思索。
venture beyond 意為「冒險超出」日常慣例或專業領域。

zh: 長久以來，人們一直認為創造力是少數人才有的特殊特質。然而，根據大量科學與社會學研究，創造力與其說是稀有天才的標誌，不如說是人類天生的潛能。因此，創造力是可以被培養與鼓勵的。
一般認為，暫時離開問題休息一下，有助於激發靈光乍現的時刻或刺激新想法。也可以探索非傳統的解決方案。這就是為什麼世界上一些最成功的公司，例如 3M 與 Google，鼓勵員工參與各種放鬆活動，像是打彈珠台和在園區裡閒逛。在這些休息時間，心智會轉向內在，得以在潛意識中琢磨細微的意義與關聯。
另一個增進創造力的方法是冒險。這是因為許多突破都出現在人們冒險跨出日常慣例或專業領域之時。例如學習新技能，或到沒去過的國家旅行，都是可行的做法。
title: 創造力可以培養

text: Hair usually gets greasy when it has not been washed because it soaks up oil—hence the need for shampoo! {{21}} this oil-absorbing feature might not always be so great for our hygiene, it can be great for the environment.

Matter of Trust, a nonprofit organization, has an innovative solution for removing the large-scale oil spill in the Gulf of Mexico in 2010, using the ultimate renewable {{22}}: human hair, of which there is an unlimited supply. Since its founding in 1998, Matter of Trust has collected donations of human hair and animal fur to {{23}} the thousands of oil spills that happen each year. The hair and fur are made into mats and brooms and sent to {{24}} waters to absorb the oil.

Across the United States each day, 300,000 pounds of hair and fur are cut. Matter of Trust is helping organize the collection of this {{25}} hair and fur through thousands of salons, pet groomers, and ranchers. Individuals can also speak to local hair stylists and pet groomers about sending in leftover hair and fur.

qs.ex: 兩個子句形成讓步對比，While 意為「雖然」。
頭髮是取之不盡的可再生「資源」，renewable resource。
清理每年數千起漏油事件的善後，clean up after。
被污染的水域，過去分詞 polluted 作形容詞。
修剪後剩下用不到的頭髮與毛皮，unneeded 意為「不需要的」。

zh: 頭髮不洗通常會變油膩，因為它會吸附油脂，這就是需要洗髮精的原因！雖然這種吸油的特性對我們的衛生不見得那麼好，但對環境卻可能很有益。
非營利組織 Matter of Trust 提出了一個創新的方法，來清除 2010 年墨西哥灣的大規模漏油，他們使用的是終極的可再生資源：人類的頭髮，而且供應無窮無盡。自從 1998 年成立以來，Matter of Trust 蒐集了捐贈的人類頭髮與動物毛皮，用來清理每年發生的數千起漏油事件。頭髮和毛皮被製成墊子與掃帚，送往受污染的水域吸附油污。
美國每天要剪掉 30 萬磅的頭髮與毛皮。Matter of Trust 正透過數千家美髮沙龍、寵物美容師與牧場主人，協助統籌蒐集這些用不到的頭髮與毛皮。個人也可以和當地的髮型師、寵物美容師商量，請他們把剩下的頭髮和毛皮寄給該組織。
title: 頭髮與毛皮清除浮油

text: You must have had this kind of experience: While in the middle of a normal dream, you suddenly realize that you are dreaming. This kind of dream is called a “lucid dream.” The term “lucid” means clear; lucid dreamers know that they are dreaming and {{26}} they are dreaming of. It is different from daydreaming. When a person is having a lucid dream, the person’s body is {{27}}; when a person daydreams, his/her body is awake. Thus, daydreams are really just waking thoughts. In lucid dreams, however, we are completely immersed in the dream world.

Yet, lucid dreaming is {{28}} just having a clear dream. It is your chance to play around with the extraordinary abilities buried in unused parts of your brain. {{29}}, it is a way for you to put the deepest areas of your brain to good use while you’re sleeping. You can be an everyday Jane Doe or John Smith while awake but a superhero while sleeping, {{30}} who you are in real life. All the obstacles of reality can be set aside and you are able to accomplish tasks that you could never manage in waking reality.

qs.ex: know what they are dreaming of，what 引導名詞子句並作 of 的受詞。
做清醒夢時身體在睡覺，與做白日夢時身體清醒對比，asleep。
is more than just ... 意為「不只是」，與後句「更是你的機會」呼應。
後句是對前句的換句話說，In other words。
不論現實中你是誰，都能成為超級英雄，regardless of。

zh: 你一定有過這樣的經驗：在一場平常的夢中，你突然意識到自己正在做夢。這種夢稱為「清醒夢」。「lucid」一詞的意思是清楚的；做清醒夢的人知道自己在做夢，也知道自己夢到什麼。這與白日夢不同。人在做清醒夢時，身體是睡著的；做白日夢時，身體則是醒著的。因此，白日夢其實只是清醒時的思緒。然而在清醒夢中，我們完全沉浸在夢的世界裡。
不過，清醒夢不只是做一個清楚的夢。它讓你有機會盡情運用埋藏在大腦未開發部位的非凡能力。換句話說，這是讓你在睡覺時，把大腦最深處充分利用起來的一種方式。你在清醒時可以是平凡的無名氏，睡著時卻成為超級英雄，不論現實中的你是誰。現實中的所有障礙都可以被擱置，你能完成在清醒現實中絕對辦不到的任務。
title: 清醒夢

text: Fortune cookies, commonly served after meals at Chinese restaurants in the U.S., are characterized by a fortune, which is written on a small piece of paper tucked inside the cookie. There are several {{31}} stories about the origin of the fortune cookie. None of them, however, has been proven to be entirely true.

One of these stories {{32}} the cookie’s origin back to 13th- and 14th-century China, which was then occupied by the Mongols. According to the legend, notes of {{33}} plans for a revolution to overthrow the Mongols were hidden in mooncakes that would ordinarily have been stuffed with sweet bean paste. The revolution turned out to be {{34}} and eventually led to the formation of the Ming Dynasty. This story may sound highly credible, but there seems to be no solid evidence that it inspired the creation of the {{35}} we know of today as fortune cookies.

Another {{36}} claims that David Jung, a Chinese immigrant living in Los Angeles, created the fortune cookie in 1918. Concerned about the poor people he saw wandering near his shop, he made cookies and passed them out free on the streets. Each cookie {{37}} a strip of paper inside with an inspirational Bible quotation on it.

However, the more generally accepted story is that the fortune cookie first {{38}} in either 1907 or 1914 in San Francisco, created by a Japanese immigrant, Makoto Hagiwara. The fortune cookie was based on a Japanese snack, but Hagiwara sweetened the recipe to appeal to American {{39}}. He enclosed thank-you notes in the cookies and served them to his guests with tea. Within a few years, Chinese restaurant owners in San Francisco had copied the recipe and {{40}} the thank-you notes with fortune notes. Such fortune cookies became common in Chinese restaurants in the U.S. after World War II.

qs.ex: 形容詞 competing，several competing stories 意為「幾個互相競爭的說法」。
動詞第三人稱單數 traces，trace ... back to 意為「追溯到」。
形容詞 secret，secret plans 意為「祕密計畫」。
形容詞 successful，革命成功並促成明朝建立。
名詞 treats，指「點心」，the treats we know as fortune cookies。
名詞 account，another account 意為「另一種說法」。
動詞過去式 contained，each cookie contained a strip of paper。
動詞過去式 appeared，first appeared in 意為「首次出現於」。
名詞複數 tastes，appeal to American tastes 意為「迎合美國人口味」。
動詞過去分詞 replaced，replaced A with B 意為「用 B 取代 A」。

zh: 幸運籤餅通常在美國的中國餐館餐後供應，特色是一張寫有籤語的小紙條，塞在餅乾裡面。關於幸運籤餅的起源有好幾種互相競爭的說法，然而沒有一種被證實完全屬實。
其中一種說法把餅乾的起源追溯到 13、14 世紀的中國，當時中國被蒙古人統治。根據傳說，寫有推翻蒙古人之革命祕密計畫的紙條，被藏在原本通常包著甜豆沙的月餅裡。這場革命後來成功了，並最終促成明朝的建立。這個故事聽起來可信度很高，但似乎沒有確切證據顯示它啟發了我們今天所知的幸運籤餅這種點心的誕生。
另一種說法聲稱，住在洛杉磯的華人移民傑恩（David Jung）於 1918 年發明了幸運籤餅。他關心那些在店附近遊蕩的窮人，便做餅乾在街上免費發送。每塊餅乾裡都有一張紙條，上面寫著激勵人心的聖經語錄。
然而，較普遍為人接受的說法是，幸運籤餅最早於 1907 或 1914 年出現在舊金山，由日本移民萩原真所創。幸運籤餅是以日本點心為基礎，但萩原把配方改甜，以迎合美國人的口味。他把感謝字條放進餅乾裡，與茶一起端給客人。幾年之內，舊金山的中國餐館老闆就複製了這個配方，並用籤語取代了感謝字條。二次大戰後，這種幸運籤餅在美國的中國餐館中變得很常見。
title: 幸運籤餅的起源

text: April Fools’ Day, one of the most light-hearted days of the year, has an unclear origin. Some see it as a celebration related to the turn of the seasons from winter to spring; others, however, believe that it {{16}} the adoption of a new calendar.

Ancient cultures celebrated New Year’s Day on or around April 1, which roughly coincides with the beginning of spring. In 1582, Pope Gregory XIII ordered a new calendar, which called for New Year’s Day to be celebrated on January 1. However, many people, either refusing to accept the new date or not having heard about it, {{17}} to celebrate New Year’s Day on April 1. Other people began to make fun of these traditionalists, sending them on “fool’s errands” or trying to fool them into believing something false. {{18}}, the practice spread throughout Europe and the rest of the world.

Nowadays, on April Fools’ Day, people often {{19}} to create elaborate hoaxes to fool others. Newspapers, radio and TV stations, and websites have participated in the April 1 tradition of making {{20}} reports in order to fool their audiences. The BBC once reported that Swiss farmers were experiencing a spaghetti crop and showed scenes of people harvesting noodles from trees. Guess what? Numerous viewers were fooled.

qs.ex: 有人認為愚人節源自新曆的採用，stem from 意為「源自」。
主詞 many people 之後插入分詞片語，主要動詞用過去式 continued。
這種習俗「最終」傳遍歐洲與世界各地，Eventually。
