人們不惜大費周章編造精心的騙局，go to great lengths。
為了愚弄觀眾而製作「虛構的」報導，fictional。

zh: 愚人節是一年中最輕鬆愉快的日子之一，起源並不明確。有些人認為它是與冬去春來的季節轉換有關的慶祝活動；然而也有人認為它源自新曆法的採用。
古代文化在 4 月 1 日前後慶祝新年，這大致與春天開始的時間相符。1582 年，教宗格雷果里十三世下令採用新曆，規定新年應在 1 月 1 日慶祝。然而，許多人有的拒絕接受新日期，有的根本沒聽說，仍然繼續在 4 月 1 日慶祝新年。其他人開始取笑這些守舊者，派他們去做「傻瓜差事」，或試圖騙他們相信假的事。最終，這種習俗傳遍了歐洲和世界其他地方。
如今在愚人節，人們常常不惜大費周章，編造精心設計的惡作劇來愚弄別人。報紙、電台、電視台和網站都參與了 4 月 1 日製作虛構報導來愚弄觀眾的傳統。英國廣播公司（BBC）曾報導瑞士農民正迎來義大利麵大豐收，並播出人們從樹上採收麵條的畫面。你猜結果如何？許多觀眾都被騙了。
title: 愚人節的起源

text: The pineapple, a delicious tropical fruit, has been valued for centuries not only for its distinct and unique taste, but also for its miraculous health and medical benefits. But pineapples can also be a fashionable fruit: Pineapple leaves can {{21}} a substitute for leather.

The idea was developed when a Spanish designer travelling to the Philippines observed a traditional Filipino shirt {{22}} together with the fibers of pineapple leaves. After five years of research, she created from pineapple leaves a material which, like real leather, can be used for making bags, shoes, and {{23}} textile products. It is an eco-friendly and biodegradable fiber.

This eco-friendly leather has clear {{24}} for the environment, compared to real leather and synthetic leathers. It requires fewer chemicals, making it safer for the workers in factories. Its manufacture also leaves a smaller carbon footprint. In addition, the leftover material following the removal of fibers can even be used as a natural fertilizer back in the pineapple fields.
{{25}} its low cost, this innovative material is already being used by many leading fashion companies to make their products.

qs.ex: 鳳梨葉可「充當」皮革的替代品，serve as。
shirt woven together with fibers，過去分詞表被動，修飾 shirt。
bags, shoes, and other textile products 意為「其他紡織品」。
與真皮相比，對環境有明顯「優勢」，clear advantages。
因為低成本，所以被許多品牌採用，Due to 表原因。

zh: 鳳梨是一種美味的熱帶水果，數百年來不僅因其獨特的風味，也因其神奇的健康與醫療益處而受到重視。但鳳梨也可以是一種時尚的水果：鳳梨葉可以充當皮革的替代品。
這個點子是在一位西班牙設計師前往菲律賓旅行，看到一件用鳳梨葉纖維編織而成的傳統菲律賓襯衫時發展出來的。經過五年的研究，她用鳳梨葉製造出一種材料，與真皮一樣，可以用來製作包包、鞋子和其他紡織品。這是一種環保且可生物分解的纖維。
與真皮及合成皮革相比，這種環保皮革對環境有明顯的優勢。它需要的化學物質較少，使工廠工人更安全。它的製造過程也留下較小的碳足跡。此外，取出纖維後剩下的材料，甚至還能作為天然肥料回到鳳梨田裡使用。
由於成本低廉，許多一流的時尚公司已經用這種創新材料來製作產品。
title: 鳳梨葉人造皮革

text: Researchers from a university in Japan have developed “diet-glasses” that play tricks with one’s perception of food, which could be helpful to people on a diet. A camera and a viewing system are built {{26}} these glasses. As the wearer brings the food toward their mouth, the camera captures an image of the food. It replays the image back through the glasses after processing it on an attached computer. The size of the food they are about to eat is magnified while {{27}} of their hand remains normal. Their brain is {{28}} tricked into thinking they are eating more than they really are. The study showed that participants who wore the glasses ate 9.3% less than those who did not wear them.

The team has also developed a special device which uses scent bottles and visual trickery to make the wearers of these glasses think that the plain snack they are eating is {{29}} than it actually is. The device, for instance, can be set to {{30}} one’s favorite flavor. Recent experiments with this device showed that 80% of the participants were fooled by the smell. For example, some participants thought that they were eating a chocolate snack, but in fact they were not.

qs.ex: 相機與顯示系統被「內建於」眼鏡中，be built into。
that 代替前面的 the size，that of their hand 意為「手的大小」。
食物看起來變大，因此大腦被騙，Therefore 表結果。
用氣味騙人，讓人覺得點心比實際更「美味」，與後面的口味呼應。
裝置可設定為「釋放」出喜歡的口味（氣味）。

zh: 日本一所大學的研究人員開發出一種「減肥眼鏡」，能讓人對食物產生錯覺，可能對正在節食的人有所幫助。眼鏡中內建了相機與顯示系統。當佩戴者把食物送向嘴邊時，相機會拍下食物的影像，經連接的電腦處理後，再透過眼鏡重新播放出來。他們即將吃下的食物大小被放大，而他們手的大小則保持正常。因此，他們的大腦被騙，以為自己吃的比實際上更多。研究顯示，戴眼鏡的受試者比沒戴的人少吃了 9.3%。
研究團隊還開發了一種特殊裝置，利用香味瓶與視覺把戲，讓佩戴這種眼鏡的人以為他們所吃的普通點心比實際上更美味。例如，這個裝置可以設定成釋放出使用者最愛的口味。最近用這個裝置進行的實驗顯示，80% 的參與者被氣味所騙。例如，有些參與者以為自己吃的是巧克力點心，但事實上並不是。
title: 減肥眼鏡

text: My father started to suffer from memory loss right after his marriage. Or so my mother told us. She said they were married on May 26, while my dad’s memory told him it was June 25. This often {{31}} their anniversary celebration, for his rose bouquet always came one month late. Mom seldom asked Dad to go shopping in the traditional market for her. But whenever Dad {{32}} on going, she made sure that he brought a shopping list. Dad certainly had the list {{33}} when he left for the market, but he would somehow forget it, and then would find it again only after he returned home. Of course, the {{34}} that he made were based mainly on his memory of the list. Unfortunately, the items were usually different from Mom’s {{35}}.

My father’s poor memory gave him certain advantages, though. For instance, he was {{36}} with many secrets in my family and our community. Because of his poor memory, he had the {{37}} of hearing everyone’s private matters. The reason was {{38}}: Dad would not remember any of it, we thought. As for our neighbors, they liked to invite my father to dinner so that they could tell him stories about their children, parents, friends, and pets. They also believed the secrets in their families would never be {{39}}. They were quite right, for my father cared {{40}} about who did what to whom. But there is one thing he would never forget: showing up for dinner on time.

qs.ex: 動詞過去式 ruined，這常「毀了」他們的結婚紀念日慶祝（玫瑰晚一個月）。
insisted on going，insist on 意為「堅持」，用過去式。
形容詞 ready，had the list ready 意為「備妥清單」。
名詞複數 purchases，他買的東西，指購買的物品。
名詞複數 requests，與媽媽的「要求」不同。

名詞 privilege，the privilege of hearing 意為「聽到的特權」。

過去分詞 revealed，祕密絕不會被「洩漏」，be revealed。

zh: 我父親在婚後不久就開始記憶衰退。至少我母親是這麼告訴我們的。她說他們是 5 月 26 日結婚，而爸爸的記憶卻告訴他是 6 月 25 日。這經常毀了他們的結婚紀念日慶祝，因為他的玫瑰花束總是晚一個月才來。媽媽很少叫爸爸去傳統市場幫她買東西。但每當爸爸堅持要去時，她都會確保他帶著購物清單。爸爸出門去市場時，確實有備妥清單，但不知怎麼就是會忘記帶，然後直到回家後才又找到。當然，他所買的東西主要是憑他對清單的記憶。可惜的是，那些東西通常和媽媽的要求不同。
不過，我父親的壞記性也給了他某些好處。例如，他受託保管我們家與社區的許多祕密。由於他記性不好，他有聽到每個人私事的特權。原因很明顯：我們認為爸爸一件也記不住。至於鄰居們，他們喜歡邀請我父親去吃晚飯，好對他講述關於他們的孩子、父母、朋友和寵物的故事。他們也相信自己家裡的祕密永遠不會被洩漏。他們想得一點也沒錯，因為我父親毫不在乎誰對誰做了什麼。但有一件事他絕不會忘記：準時出現在晚餐桌上。
title: 記性不好的爸爸

text: The art and tradition of using all-natural paste from the henna plant to create temporary henna tattoos goes back to ancient Asia and the Middle East. Over the centuries, henna tattoos {{16}} used in weddings and holiday celebrations because they are thought to carry blessings from the gods. Today, the ancient art form has found a new {{17}} in the hands of contemporary artists.

Henna Heals, an artist group based in Canada, uses henna tattoos to help women suffering from cancer feel confident and beautiful again. They draw elegant henna crowns on the women’s bare heads to help them {{18}} the loss of their hair after cancer treatment. Featuring floral patterns, religious symbols, and messages of hope, the painted henna crowns are amazing substitutes for the hats and wigs that the cancer patients would {{19}} use to cover their heads. Many women report that the henna crowns really work as a healing device, helping them build a more {{20}} self-image at a time when they are vulnerable and depressed. According to Frances Darwin, founder of Henna Heals, the number of artists now involved in the project across Canada and the US has grown to over 150.

qs.ex: 「Over the centuries」在此指從過去持續到現在的時間，需用現在完成式 have been used（被動），故選 have been。
found a new application 意指古老技藝在當代藝術家手中有了新的「應用」，application 最符合文意。
cope with the loss of their hair 表示「應付、面對掉髮的打擊」，cope with 為適當搭配。
would otherwise use 表示「否則（若沒有彩繪頭冠）會使用的帽子與假髮」，副詞 otherwise 符合語意。
幫助患者建立更「正向的」自我形象，與後面 vulnerable and depressed 形成對比，故選 positive。

zh: 用天然的指甲花（散沫花）膏在身上畫出暫時性刺青的藝術與傳統，可追溯至古代亞洲與中東。數世紀以來，指甲花刺青一直被用於婚禮與節慶，因為人們認為它能帶來神明的祝福。如今，這項古老的藝術在當代藝術家的手中找到了新的應用。

總部位於加拿大的藝術家團體「Henna Heals」運用指甲花刺青，幫助罹癌的女性重拾自信與美麗。他們在女性光禿的頭上畫出優雅的指甲花頭冠，幫助她們面對癌症治療後掉髮的失落。這些彩繪頭冠以花卉圖案、宗教符號與充滿希望的語句為特色，是癌症患者原本會用來遮蓋頭部的帽子與假髮的絕佳替代品。許多女性表示，指甲花頭冠確實有療癒的效果，在她們脆弱又沮喪的時候，幫助她們建立更正面的自我形象。根據 Henna Heals 創辦人 Frances Darwin 所說，目前加拿大與美國參與這項計畫的藝術家人數已增加到一百五十多人。
title: 指甲花刺青與癌症患者

text: When a person sneezes, the droplets can spread diseases. Now research shows that plants have a somewhat {{21}} problem. Plant diseases can also spread through tiny water drops that jump off leaves—a plant’s version of a sneeze.

Scientists already knew earlier that wind and splashes of rainwater can move bacteria and other germs from leaf to leaf. {{22}} other possible transmission routes, researchers at Virginia Tech observed water drops on the leaves of wheat plants that were infected with leaf rust. They found that the sick plants could “sneeze” and {{23}} tiny water drops filled with leaf rust germs, spreading the disease to neighboring plants.

The researchers noticed that small drops of water on the wheat leaves would move to combine and form a larger drop. As they were moving, the energy of the droplets in motion would be released. This energy allowed the water {{24}} into the air, which looked just like sneezing!

However, not all plants can sneeze. The ability is {{25}} to those with leaves that are hydrophobic, or repel water—a special feature that forces the liquid to move away when the leaf is exposed to it.

qs.ex: 前句說人打噴嚏會傳播疾病，植物也有「類似的」問題，故選 similar。
researchers 為了「尋找」其他可能的傳播途徑而觀察，in a search for 後接名詞片語，符合文意。
sick plants 能「噴射出」帶有病菌的小水滴，shoot out 語意最貼切。
allow + 受詞 + to V，故 allow the water to jump into the air，選 to jump。
後文指只有葉片具疏水性的植物才能「打噴嚏」，表示此能力為這類植物「所獨有」，be unique to 為正確搭配。

zh: 人打噴嚏時，飛沫會傳播疾病。如今研究顯示，植物也有幾分類似的問題。植物疾病同樣可以透過從葉片上彈跳起來的微小水滴傳播，這就是植物版的「打噴嚏」。
科學家先前就知道，風和飛濺的雨水可以把細菌及其他病原體從一片葉子帶到另一片葉子。為了尋找其他可能的傳播途徑，維吉尼亞理工大學的研究人員觀察了感染葉鏽病的小麥葉片上的水滴。他們發現，生病的植物會「打噴嚏」，噴射出充滿葉鏽病菌的微小水滴，把疾病傳給鄰近的植物。
研究人員注意到，小麥葉片上的小水滴會移動並合併成較大的水滴。在移動的過程中，水滴運動的能量會被釋放出來。這股能量使水滴得以彈到空中，看起來就像打噴嚏一樣！
不過，並非所有植物都會打噴嚏。這種能力只有葉片具疏水性（即排斥水）的植物才有，這項特殊性質會在葉片接觸到液體時，迫使液體移開。
title: 植物也會打噴嚏

text: The idea of Blue Monday dates back to a 2005 campaign by Sky Travel. The travel company wanted to {{26}} people to take January vacations, so they reached out to a psychologist. The scholar then developed an equation to find the most depressing day of the year, and it turned out to be the third Monday in January. Since then, other companies have jumped on the bandwagon to promote everything from soft drinks to new clothes as a {{27}}. A group in the UK even started a website devoted to “beating Blue Monday.”

Many scientists, however, say there is no evidence that Blue Monday causes any more sadness than other specific days of the year. {{28}}, the idea of Blue Monday persists. According to psychologist Dean Burnett, people feel down in January {{29}} post-holiday discontent, and the Blue Monday claim makes it seem like there are scientific reasons for this. Also, the idea {{30}} a very complex issue regarding depression into something simple and easily understandable, and that tends to appeal to a lot of people.

qs.ex: 旅行社希望「鼓勵」人們在一月去度假，encourage + 人 + to V 為正確結構。
各家公司把飲料、新衣說成是對付「藍色星期一」憂鬱的「解方」，故選 remedy。
前句說科學家認為毫無證據，後句說這個概念依然存在，語氣轉折，用 And yet「然而」。
人們一月心情低落「是由於」節後的不滿，owing to 表原因。
把複雜的憂鬱議題「簡化」成簡單易懂的東西，break down 在此指將複雜事物拆解、簡化，符合文意。

zh: 「藍色星期一」的概念可追溯至 2005 年 Sky Travel 的一項宣傳活動。這家旅遊公司想鼓勵人們在一月份去度假，於是找上了一位心理學家。這位學者接著設計出一個方程式，找出一年中最令人沮喪的一天，結果是一月的第三個星期一。從那時起，其他公司也紛紛跟風，把從汽水到新衣的各種商品都宣傳為對付藍色星期一的解方。英國甚至有一個團體架設了專門「擊退藍色星期一」的網站。
然而，許多科學家指出，沒有證據顯示藍色星期一比一年中其他特定日子帶來更多悲傷。儘管如此，藍色星期一的說法依然流傳。根據心理學家 Dean Burnett 的說法，人們在一月感到低落是因為假期結束後的不滿情緒，而藍色星期一的說法讓這種情緒看似有科學上的原因。此外，這個說法把與憂鬱症有關的一個非常複雜的議題簡化成簡單易懂的東西，這往往能吸引許多人。
title: 藍色星期一

text: Dimples are small folds or indentations on the cheeks of one’s face. Generally, they appear on both cheeks; a single dimple on one cheek is a relatively {{31}} phenomenon. Some cultures are found to show preference for dimples on one’s cheeks, as the feature is claimed to be a sign of {{32}}.

Though often associated with beauty, most dimples are actually a genetic {{33}} caused by shortened facial muscles. When a person smiles, the shorter-than-normal muscle pulls up the facial skin, which in turn creates a small indentation—or dimple—in the skin. Such dimples tend to occur in families, and are assumed to be an inherited feature. In fact, some researchers believe that the {{34}} of dimples from parents to children takes only one gene. If neither of the parents has dimple genes, their children will not {{35}} the trait.

Not all dimples are formed by a genetic defect, though; some may appear due to the {{36}} of excessive fat on the face. Such dimples are not a permanent trait, for they vanish when the excessive fat goes away. Many babies, for example, have dimples on their {{37}} cheeks. As they grow older and lose their baby fat, the dimples may {{38}} with time.

For those people who were born without {{39}} dimples, various methods can be applied to successfully create them. These methods {{40}} from a simple step like makeup to a drastic one like surgery. It all depends on whether you think it is worth the effort.

qs.ex: 前面 a relatively ___ phenomenon 指單邊酒窩較少見，需形容詞，選 rare。
某些文化偏好酒窩，因其被認為是（名詞）「魅力」的象徵，選 attractiveness。
後文說酒窩是由肌肉縮短造成的基因「缺陷」，a genetic 後需名詞，選 flaw。
from parents to children 表示基因的「傳遞」，需名詞 transfer（the transfer of ... from ... to ...）。
will not 後接原形動詞，意為子女不會「表現出」該特徵，選動詞 exhibit。
due to the 後需名詞，指臉上過多脂肪的「存在」，選 presence。
嬰兒的臉頰有酒窩，與 baby fat 呼應，需形容詞「圓潤的」，選 chubby。
隨著脂肪減少，酒窩可能隨時間「消失」，需原形動詞 fade。
天生沒有「天然的」酒窩，與後面人工製造酒窩對比，需形容詞 natural。
these methods 為主詞，後接 from ... to ... 表「範圍涵蓋」，複數主詞用原形動詞 range。

zh: 酒窩是臉頰上的小皺褶或凹陷。一般來說，酒窩會出現在雙頰；只有單邊臉頰有酒窩則是相對罕見的現象。人們發現有些文化偏愛臉頰上的酒窩，因為據說這項特徵是有魅力的象徵。
雖然酒窩常與美麗連在一起，但大多數酒窩其實是由臉部肌肉縮短所造成的基因缺陷。當一個人微笑時，比正常短的肌肉會把臉部皮膚往上拉，進而在皮膚上形成小小的凹陷，也就是酒窩。這類酒窩往往在家族中出現，被認為是遺傳特徵。事實上，一些研究人員認為，酒窩從父母傳給子女只需要一個基因。如果父母雙方都沒有酒窩基因，他們的孩子就不會表現出這項特徵。
不過，並非所有酒窩都是由基因缺陷造成的；有些酒窩可能是因為臉上有過多脂肪而出現。這類酒窩不是永久的特徵，因為多餘的脂肪消失後，酒窩也會隨之消失。例如，許多嬰兒的圓潤臉頰上有酒窩。隨著他們長大、褪去嬰兒肥，酒窩可能會隨時間逐漸消失。
對於那些天生沒有天然酒窩的人，可以採用各種方法成功製造出酒窩。這些方法從化妝這種簡單的步驟，到手術這種激進的手段都有。這一切都取決於你是否認為這樣的努力值得。
title: 酒窩的成因

text: Street pigeons are a common sight in many European cities. In fact, a visit to a major European city just would not be the same {{16}} encountering them: bathing in fountains, perching on historic buildings, and flocking in public squares. In Barcelona, however, the birds are now threatening to {{17}} the city’s historic center, pooping on monuments, buildings, and even tourists.

The city council originally proposed {{18}} the pigeon population by gathering the birds and shooting them. But that idea led to strong protests from numerous animal rights groups. After heated debates and discussions, the government was finally persuaded to consider another {{19}} effective method: giving the pigeons birth control.

In 2016, the city council decided to put its 85,000 pigeon population on a birth control pill to block the formation of eggs in birds. Starting from April 2017, the pills were placed in 40 bird feeders {{20}} throughout the city. It was predicted that there would be a decrease of 20 percent in the pigeon population in the first year and between 70 and 80 percent in four or five years.

qs.ex: 「不會一樣」是因為「沒有」遇見牠們，without + 動名詞 encountering 符合語意。
鳥群威脅要「占領」歷史中心，take over 最符合文意。
propose + V-ing，且目的為「減少」鴿群數量，選 reducing。
another similarly effective method 指「同樣有效的」另一種方法，副詞 similarly 修飾 effective。
bird feeders 與 install 為被動關係，過去分詞 installed 作後位修飾語。

zh: 流浪鴿是許多歐洲城市的常見景象。事實上，造訪歐洲大城市時，若沒見到牠們在噴泉裡洗澡、停在歷史建築上、成群聚集在公共廣場，總會覺得少了點什麼。然而在巴塞隆納，這些鳥如今威脅著要占領市中心的歷史區，在古蹟、建築物，甚至遊客身上大便。
市議會最初提議以捕捉並射殺的方式減少鴿子的數量。但這個想法引來許多動物保護團體的強烈抗議。經過激烈的辯論與討論後，政府終於被說服去考慮另一個同樣有效的方法：替鴿子節育。
2016 年，市議會決定讓城內八萬五千隻鴿子服用避孕藥，以阻止鳥類形成卵。從 2017 年 4 月開始，這些藥丸被放進全市各處安裝的 40 個餵鳥器中。據預測，第一年鴿子數量會減少 20%，四、五年內則會減少 70% 到 80%。
title: 巴塞隆納鴿子節育

text: Being hit by lightning is a rare event. Over the course of an 80-year life span, the odds of being hit by lightning are 1 in 3,000, {{21}} the probability of being struck seven different times. Roy Sullivan, a park ranger in the United States, was struck by lightning more recorded times than any other human being. Over his 36-year career, Sullivan was struck by lightning seven times—and {{22}} each shock!

Strikes one, two, and three were pure bad luck, he thought. But after strike four, Sullivan became {{23}} death and took precautions during lightning strikes. Strike five occurred in 1973 when Sullivan was on patrol. A storm cloud “chased” him until he was struck. The same thing happened again in 1976. Sullivan, while surveying a campground, felt that a cloud was {{24}} him, and tried all he could to run—but it got him anyway. Finally, on 25 June 1977, a seventh and final bolt struck Sullivan as he was fishing in a pond. “I don’t believe God is after me,” he theorized. “If he was, the first bolt {{25}} enough. Best I can figure is that I have some chemical, some mineral, in my body that draws lightning. I just wish I knew.”

qs.ex: 被雷擊中一次已罕見，更「不用說」被擊中七次的機率，not to mention 表示「更別提」。
被雷擊七次「卻都活了下來」，survived each shock 符合文意。
第四次後他開始「害怕」死亡並採取預防措施，be fearful of 表示畏懼。
雲似乎在「追著」他，與前文 chased 呼應，coming after him 即「追趕他」。
混合假設：If he was (after me) 與現在事實相反，主句則與過去事實相反，用 would have been enough，表示第一次雷擊就已足夠。

zh: 被雷擊中是罕見的事。在八十年的壽命中，被雷擊中的機率是三千分之一，更別提被擊中七次的機率了。美國的公園巡警 Roy Sullivan 有紀錄的被雷擊次數比任何人都多。在他三十六年的職業生涯中，Sullivan 被雷擊中七次，而且每一次電擊他都活了下來！

他認為，前三次雷擊純粹是運氣不好。但第四次之後，Sullivan 開始害怕死亡，並在打雷時採取預防措施。第五次發生在 1973 年，當時 Sullivan 正在巡邏。一朵風暴雲「追著」他，直到他被擊中。1976 年又發生了同樣的事。Sullivan 在勘查一處露營地時，感覺有朵雲正追著他，他拚命想跑，但還是被擊中了。最後，在 1977 年 6 月 25 日，第七道也是最後一道閃電擊中了正在池塘釣魚的 Sullivan。「我不相信上帝在找我麻煩，」他推測道，「如果祂真的要找我，第一道閃電就夠了。我能想到最好的解釋是，我體內有某種化學物質、某種礦物質會吸引閃電。真希望我知道答案。」
title: 被雷劈七次的人

text: Glaciers are usually associated with colder climates. But some mountain ranges of South America, Africa, and Indonesia are also {{26}} glaciers and ice sheets. These tropical glaciers serve as a major source of water supply to one-sixth of the world’s population.

A newly published study, however, revealed that rising temperatures are posing an {{27}} threat to the last tropical glaciers in Indonesia’s Papua region. The ice sheets, which once spanned 20 square kilometers, are thinning over five times as quickly compared to a few years ago. {{28}} already shrunk by 85% to a mere 0.5 square kilometers, Papua’s glaciers will completely disappear within a decade, researchers have predicted.

The disappearance of the glaciers will also leave a significant {{29}} impact. For many indigenous Papuans, the ice sheets represent a sacred symbol. “The mountains and valleys are the arms and legs of their god and the glaciers are the head,” explained the head researcher.

The study warned that Papua’s glaciers are only the “first to go” if greenhouse gases are {{30}} and temperatures continue rising. And this is certainly a serious warning about the depressing fate of other glaciers around the world.

qs.ex: be home to 表示「是……的所在地」，南美、非洲、印尼的山脈也有冰河。
氣溫上升對冰河構成「迫在眉睫的」威脅，immediate threat 為常見搭配。
此為分詞構句，由 Because they have already shrunk 簡化而來，shrink 為不及物動詞，glaciers 與 shrink 為主動關係，用完成式分詞 Having already shrunk，意為「已經縮小」。
後文談到冰河對巴布亞原住民是神聖象徵，屬於「文化上的」衝擊，選 cultural。
若溫室氣體「不受控制」而氣溫持續上升，left unchecked 表示放任不管。

zh: 冰河通常與較寒冷的氣候連在一起。但南美洲、非洲和印尼的一些山脈也有冰河與冰原。這些熱帶冰河是全球六分之一人口的主要水源。
然而，一項新發表的研究揭露，氣溫上升正對印尼巴布亞地區最後的熱帶冰河構成迫切的威脅。這些冰原曾經廣達二十平方公里，現在變薄的速度是幾年前的五倍多。巴布亞的冰河已經縮小了 85%，只剩下區區 0.5 平方公里；研究人員預測，這些冰河將在十年內完全消失。
冰河的消失也將帶來重大的文化衝擊。對許多巴布亞原住民而言，冰原是神聖的象徵。首席研究員解釋說：「山脈與山谷是他們神明的手臂與雙腿，而冰河則是頭。」
研究警告，如果對溫室氣體放任不管、氣溫持續上升，巴布亞的冰河只是「最先消失」的。這無疑是對全球其他冰河淒涼命運的嚴重警告。
title: 巴布亞熱帶冰河消失

text: If you cannot find ways to fit exercise into your busy daily schedule, don’t worry! Exercise doesn’t always have to be laborious. Research shows that {{31}} amounts of exercise—even just 15 minutes a day—helps ease depression, enhance self-image, relieve stress, and much more. That’s right. Doing exercise makes you happy, and you don’t have to be a fitness {{32}} to do it. What you need to do is to make “start slow and have fun” a motto to {{33}}. Then you’ll be well on your way to using physical activity as a tool to make you feel better every day.

The “no pain, no gain” view of exercise is now considered old-fashioned. In fact, {{34}} health studies prove that exercise doesn’t have to hurt to be effective. You might {{35}} that if working out doesn’t give you pain, it isn’t working. According to fitness trainers, physically {{36}} exercises may make you breathe heavily and your muscles may ache temporarily, but exercise should not be painful. In fact, if it is, it may {{37}} an injury or muscle strain. Many great forms of exercise—like walking, swimming, or gentle stretching—get results without the {{38}} or discomfort some people associate with exercise.

For the sake of your health, it is time to make regular exercise a part of your life. Keep in mind that even short periods of low-impact exercise serve as a powerful {{39}} to improve your health. So, no matter how busy you are, try to {{40}} for exercise every day, like a 15-minute walk with your dog. Your body will thank you in many ways.

zh: 如果你找不到方法把運動塞進繁忙的日常行程，別擔心！運動不一定都要很費力。研究顯示，適量的運動，即使一天只有 15 分鐘，也有助於緩解憂鬱、增強自我形象、紓解壓力等等。沒錯，運動讓你快樂，而且你不必是健身狂熱者也能做到。你需要做的，是把「慢慢開始、享受樂趣」當作要遵守的座右銘。這樣你就能順利地把體能活動當作工具，讓自己每天都感覺更好。
「沒有痛苦就沒有收穫」的運動觀念現在被認為是過時的。事實上，目前的健康研究證明，運動不必痛才有效。你可能會主張，如果運動不讓你疼痛，就沒有效果。根據健身教練的說法，費力的運動可能會讓你呼吸急促、肌肉暫時痠痛，但運動不應該是痛苦的。事實上，如果會痛，那可能表示你受傷或肌肉拉傷了。許多很棒的運動，像是走路、游泳或溫和的伸展，都能達到成效，又不會帶來某些人一想到運動就聯想到的痠痛或不適。
為了你的健康，是時候讓規律運動成為你生活的一部分了。請記住，即使是短時間的低衝擊運動，也是改善健康的有力手段。所以，不管你有多忙，每天都試著抽出時間運動，例如帶著你的狗散步 15 分鐘。你的身體會在許多方面感謝你。
title: 輕鬆運動有益身心

text: A book town is a rural town in which second-hand and antiquarian bookshops are concentrated. The concept was {{11}} by Richard Booth, who opened the first second-hand bookshop in Hay-on-Wye, UK in 1961. Following him, many local people opened their own bookshops, and the small town soon became a model of sustainable rural development and tourism. Since the 1970s, book towns like Hay-on-Wye {{12}} up all over the world.

Although all book towns have a great number of bookshops, that’s where the similarities {{13}}. Each of these towns shows unique features of its own. Some have many small private shops, while others have organizations steered by volunteers. Some even run regular activities to attract visitors. For example, an annual book festival is held in Hay-on-Wye. Clunes, in Australia, holds a monthly book talk that hosts authors to discuss their latest {{14}}.

As digital reading is changing our traditional way of reading, book towns like Hay-on-Wye are particularly important to {{15}}. The feel of a book, the smell, the weight, and the knowledge that a particular book might be more than a hundred years old—all these highlight the importance of preserving the physical book as a complement to technology.

qs.ex: the concept was initiated by Richard Booth 表示「由他首創」這個概念，選 initiated。
Since the 1970s 表示從過去持續至今，用現在完成進行式 have been springing up，描述書鎮陸續冒出。

末句強調保存實體書的重要性，故書鎮對於「讓紙本文字延續下去」特別重要，選 keep the printed word alive。

zh: 書鎮是二手書店與古書店集中的鄉村小鎮。這個概念由 Richard Booth 所創，他於 1961 年在英國的海伊鎮開了第一間二手書店。繼他之後，許多當地人也開了自己的書店，這個小鎮很快就成為永續鄉村發展與觀光的典範。自 1970 年代以來，像海伊鎮這樣的書鎮在世界各地陸續興起。
雖然所有書鎮都有大量書店，但相似之處也僅止於此。每個小鎮都展現出自己的獨特風貌。有些書鎮有許多小型私人商店，有些則由志工領導的組織經營。有些甚至定期舉辦活動來吸引遊客。例如，海伊鎮每年都舉辦書展。澳洲的克盧恩斯每月舉辦一場新書講座，邀請作者來談他們的最新作品。
由於數位閱讀正在改變我們傳統的閱讀方式，像海伊鎮這樣的書鎮對於讓紙本文字延續下去格外重要。書的觸感、氣味、重量，以及知道某本書可能已有一百多年歷史，這一切都凸顯了保存實體書作為科技之補充的重要性。
title: 書鎮

text: Airline passengers may have noticed that all plane windows have rounded edges, instead of the hard corners commonly found in our house. The round windows are indeed pleasant to the eye, but they actually were designed for reasons {{16}} aesthetics.

In the early days of aviation, plane windows {{17}} square in shape. Then as commercial air travel became popular in the 1950s and airplanes began flying higher and faster, three planes mysteriously broke apart in midair. The cause? Square windows. Scientists found that sharp corners are natural weak spots where stress concentrates. The problem is {{18}} when airplanes fly at higher altitudes, where the difference between the inside and outside pressure increases, causing added stress. When subjected to repeated pressurization high in the sky, the four corners on a square window may {{19}}.

Curved windows, on the other hand, distribute stress around more evenly, reducing the likelihood of cracks or breaks. Circular shapes are also stronger and resist deformation, and therefore can {{20}} extreme differences in pressure inside and outside of an aircraft.
Thus, round windows are a major safety innovation that keeps planes from disintegrating mid-flight. They are also used on ships and spacecraft for their greater structural integrity.

zh: 搭飛機的乘客可能已經注意到，所有飛機的窗戶都是圓角的，而不是我們家中常見的尖銳直角。圓形窗戶確實賞心悅目，但它們其實是出於美觀以外的理由而設計的。
在航空業早期，飛機窗戶是方形的。後來到了 1950 年代，商業航空旅行開始流行，飛機也飛得更高更快，結果有三架飛機在半空中離奇解體。原因是什麼？方形窗戶。科學家發現，尖角是應力集中的天然弱點。當飛機在更高的高度飛行時，這個問題會加劇，因為機艙內外的壓力差增大，造成額外的應力。在高空中反覆受到加壓時，方形窗戶的四個角可能會釀成災難。
相對地，弧形窗戶能更平均地分散應力，降低出現裂縫或破裂的可能性。圓形也更堅固、能抵抗變形，因此能承受機艙內外的極端壓力差。
因此，圓形窗戶是一項重大的安全創新，能避免飛機在飛行途中解體。由於結構完整性更佳，船舶與太空船也使用圓形窗戶。
title: 飛機為何用圓窗

text: A stunt person is a man or a woman who performs dangerous acts, usually in the television or movie industry. In this line of work, the person is paid to do daring actions that are deemed too {{21}} for the regular actor to perform, including jumping from heights, crashing cars, or fighting with weapons.

Stunt work emerged out of {{22}} over time. In the early days of the film industry, actors themselves shot acrobatic acts and dangerous scenes, until they began to get injured. There were, however, no {{23}} crew members to perform impressive stunts at that time. If something dangerous needed to be done for a scene, the producers would hire anyone crazy or desperate enough to do it. These people were not trained to perform stunts, so they often {{24}} things for the first time during the actual shooting. They had to learn from their own mistakes, which {{25}} some their lives, and almost all suffered light or severe injuries.

Beginning around 1910, audiences developed a taste for serial action movies, which {{26}} the use of dedicated stunt people to perform in dangerous scenes. Such demand increased with the rise of western movies, and many cowboys with masterful skills on horseback found a new {{27}} as a stunt person. Tom Mix and Yakima Canutt were among the most famous. The 1960s and ’70s {{28}} the development of most modern stunt technology, like air rams and bullet squibs. That technology has continued to evolve into the present.

Today, CGI (computer generated imagery) is widely used in filmmaking, and it is now {{29}} to create very lifelike scenes without using real stunt people. However, CGI has difficulties of its own, and there will always be a demand for the realism and thrilling {{30}} of an actual stunt. So the stunt industry is probably in no immediate danger of dying off.

zh: 特技演員是表演危險動作的男性或女性，通常在電視或電影產業工作。在這個行業中，這些人受雇去做被認為對一般演員來說太危險的大膽動作，包括從高處跳下、撞車，或是持武器打鬥。
特技工作是隨著時間因需要而產生的。在電影業的早期，演員自己拍攝雜技動作和危險場面，直到他們開始受傷。然而，當時並沒有專業的工作人員來表演令人驚艷的特技。如果某個場景需要做危險的事，製片人就會雇用任何瘋狂或走投無路到願意去做的人。這些人沒有受過特技表演訓練，所以他們常常在實際拍攝時才第一次嘗試。他們得從自己的錯誤中學習，這讓一些人丟了性命，而且幾乎所有人都受了輕傷或重傷。
大約從 1910 年開始，觀眾對連續動作片產生了興趣，而這類電影需要專門的特技演員來演出危險場景。隨著西部片的興起，這樣的需求增加，許多擁有精湛騎術的牛仔也找到了特技演員這個新職業。Tom Mix 和 Yakima Canutt 是其中最有名的。1960 與 70 年代見證了大部分現代特技科技的發展，像是空氣彈射器與子彈爆破裝置。這些技術一直持續演進到現在。
如今，CGI（電腦生成影像）廣泛用於電影製作，現在已經可以在不使用真人特技演員的情況下創造出非常逼真的場景。然而，CGI 自身也有困難，而人們永遠會需要真實特技所帶來的逼真感與驚險刺激的感受。所以特技產業大概不會馬上面臨消亡的危機。
title: 特技演員的歷史

text: In certain forests, when you look up you will see a network of cracks formed by gaps between the outermost edges of tree branches. It looks like a precisely engineered jigsaw puzzle, each branch growing just perfectly so it almost, {{11}}, touches the neighboring tree. This beautiful phenomenon is called crown shyness.

Scientists have been discussing crown shyness since the 1920s, proposing {{12}} explanations for the phenomenon. Some researchers point out that as trees often grow close together, treetops can easily collide and break when swayed by the wind. In order to protect their branches from breakage, trees maintain “shyness gaps”—spaces large enough to prevent them from touching their neighbors.

Other scientists suggest that plants, like animals, {{13}} resources—nutrients, water, space, and light. In forested areas with thick tree crowns, there is intense struggle for these resources. Gaps in the treetops resulting from crown shyness may allow trees to increase their {{14}} light and enhance photosynthesis. Additionally, by having branches that do not touch those of their neighbors, trees may be able to limit the spread of leaf-eating insects, and potentially also the transmission of diseases from tree to tree. {{15}} decades of investigation, there is no consensus on exactly what causes the beautiful and mysterious phenomenon of crown shyness.

zh: 在某些森林裡，抬頭往上看，你會看到樹枝最外緣之間的空隙交織成網狀的裂縫。它看起來就像一幅精密設計的拼圖，每根樹枝都長得恰到好處，幾乎碰到、但又沒有真的碰到鄰近的樹。這種美麗的現象稱為「樹冠羞避」。
自 1920 年代以來，科學家就一直在討論樹冠羞避，並針對這個現象提出多種解釋。有些研究人員指出，由於樹木常常長得很近，樹梢在被風吹動時很容易相撞而折斷。為了保護樹枝不折斷，樹木會保留「羞避縫隙」，也就是寬到足以防止它們碰到鄰居的空間。
其他科學家認為，植物就像動物一樣，會為了資源（養分、水、空間與光線）而競爭。在樹冠濃密的森林地區，這些資源的爭奪十分激烈。樹冠羞避所造成的樹梢縫隙，可能讓樹木接收到更多光照，並增強光合作用。此外，由於樹枝不碰到鄰近樹木的枝條，樹木或許能限制食葉昆蟲的擴散，甚至可能還能限制疾病在樹與樹之間的傳播。儘管經過數十年的研究，對於究竟是什麼造成了樹冠羞避這種美麗又神祕的現象，仍沒有共識。
title: 樹冠羞避現象

text: Gravity has been at the top of the science agenda since the start of Mars missions. In the earlier days of space travel, scientists tried to overcome the force of gravity so that a rocket could shoot {{16}} Earth’s pull in order to land humans on the moon. Today, they are more interested in how reduced gravity affects the astronauts’ {{17}} condition.

Our bodies have evolved to exist within Earth’s gravity (1 g), not in the weightlessness of space (0 g) or the microgravity of Mars (0.3 g). When on Earth, we have more fluids in our lower body because they are pulled down by Earth’s gravity. However, with the absence of gravity in the outer space, our body fluids {{18}}, shifting toward the upper body and the head. As a result, the astronauts have swollen, puffy faces, very much resembling that of the round-headed Charlie Brown in the famous comic strip. This “Charlie Brown effect” will be more {{19}} when the astronauts go on their Mars missions, which will take about three years to complete, much longer than missions to the moon. Moreover, the effect is often {{20}} space motion sickness, headaches, and nausea. Such a syndrome is considered the top health risk for the astronauts, and scientists are still trying to figure out how it may be prevented.

zh: 自從火星任務開始以來，重力就一直是科學議題的首要項目。在太空旅行的早期，科學家試圖克服重力，好讓火箭能脫離地球的引力，把人類送上月球。如今，他們更感興趣的是，重力減弱如何影響太空人的身體狀況。

我們的身體已演化到適應地球的重力（1 g），而不是太空的失重狀態（0 g）或火星的微重力（0.3 g）。在地球上時，我們下半身的體液較多，因為它們被地球重力往下拉。然而，在外太空沒有重力的情況下，我們的體液會重新分布，往上半身與頭部移動。結果，太空人的臉會腫脹浮腫，非常像知名漫畫中圓頭的查理布朗。當太空人執行大約要花三年才能完成、比登月任務長得多的火星任務時，這種「查理布朗效應」會更加嚴重。此外，這種效應常伴隨著太空動暈症、頭痛與噁心。這種症候群被認為是太空人最主要的健康風險，科學家仍在設法找出預防的方法。
title: 重力與太空人健康

text: Water makes up more than half of our body weight. To sustain this amount of fluid in our bodies, plain water is considered our best choice, for it contains no sugar and no calories. Yet, is water always the healthiest drink we can {{21}}? Well, it depends on who and where we are, and what we’re doing.

Obviously, a physically {{22}} person with an outdoor job under the sun will need to drink more fluid than a desk-bound person who lives and works in an air-conditioned place. But there’s more to it than that. When a person sweats, he loses water and salt, so he needs to replace both. Replacing lost fluid with just plain water means the body has too much water and not enough salt. To {{23}} things out, the body will get rid of water by producing urine. For this reason, milk can actually be more {{24}} than drinking water. Milk naturally contains salt and lactose, a sugar which the human body needs in small amounts to help stimulate water {{25}}. Coconut water, which contains salt and carbohydrates, is also more functional than water at restoring and maintaining a normal fluid {{26}} after exercise.

For the average person, however, water remains a very good {{27}} for keeping hydrated—if you know how to drink it. The secret is: Never wait until the body is telling you you’re thirsty, since there must already have been significant changes in your body for it to eventually {{28}} your consciousness. At that point, it might be well past the best moment to take in fluid. Also, drinking a lot of liquid in one go can cause more water to {{29}} the body quickly and come out as urine. To {{30}} this, you need to drink water throughout the day to maintain your hydration levels.

qs.ex: can ___ 後接原形動詞片語，「拿取、選擇」的飲料，選 reach for。
a physically ___ person 為副詞 + 形容詞，戶外工作者「好動、活躍的」，選 active。
To ___ things out 為慣用語 even things out，意為「使之平衡」。
milk can be more ___ than water，指比水更「有效的」，形容詞 effective。
stimulate water ___ 需名詞，指促進水分「吸收」，選 absorption。
a normal fluid ___ 需名詞，指體液「狀態」，選 status。
a very good ___ 需名詞，水仍是補水的好「選擇」，選 option。
for it to eventually ___ your consciousness 需動詞，指口渴感終於「喚起」你的意識，選 alert（使警覺）。
cause more water to ___ the body，需動詞片語，水「流經」身體，選 pass through。
To ___ this 需動詞，指「對抗」這種情況，選 combat。

zh: 水占了我們體重的一半以上。為了維持體內這麼多的液體，白開水被認為是我們最好的選擇，因為它不含糖，也不含熱量。然而，水是否永遠是我們能拿來喝的最健康的飲料呢？嗯，這要看我們是誰、在哪裡，以及正在做什麼。

很明顯地，在烈日下從事戶外工作、活動量大的人，需要比在冷氣房裡生活、工作的久坐辦公者喝更多的液體。但事情不只如此。當一個人流汗時，他會流失水分和鹽分，所以兩者都需要補充。只用白開水補充流失的液體，意味著身體水分過多而鹽分不足。為了恢復平衡，身體會透過製造尿液來排出水分。因此，牛奶其實可能比喝水更有效。牛奶天然含有鹽和乳糖，乳糖是一種人體需要少量攝取的糖，有助於促進水分的吸收。含有鹽和碳水化合物的椰子水，在運動後恢復並維持正常的體液狀態方面，效果也比水更好。
然而，對一般人來說，水仍然是保持水分充足的好選擇，前提是你知道怎麼喝。祕訣是：千萬不要等到身體告訴你口渴了才喝，因為身體一定已經出現了顯著的變化，口渴的感覺才會最終喚起你的意識。到了那個時候，可能早已超過補充水分的最佳時機。此外，一次大量喝下液體，會讓更多水分迅速流過身體，並以尿液的形式排出。為了對抗這種情況，你需要在一天當中分次喝水，以維持體內的水分程度。
title: 喝水的學問

text: Mystery shoppers are paid consumers who are hired to shop in stores and collect data. They are sent to a wide variety of service-based businesses, including stores, restaurants, and banks—potentially anywhere customers are served. Sometimes referred to as secret shoppers, mystery shoppers {{11}} regular customers to purchase items, eat in restaurants, make inquiries, or return items. They grade and report on the quality of products, customer service, and environment of the stores {{12}} they are assigned.

When evaluating a business, mystery shoppers have to follow certain standard procedures to avoid {{13}}. They are often given a checklist that provides directions on what to observe or look out for to ensure consistency. Sometimes these shoppers collect data about their “normal” observations, such as cleanliness of the store or timeliness of the service. They may also pretend to be {{14}} customers, arguing with a salesperson without a good reason. With the data they collect, mystery shoppers can identify areas for {{15}} and thereby help enhance the quality of products and services. In this way, these secret shoppers may help a business gain a competitive edge.

qs.ex: 「秘密客」是假扮成一般顧客去購物、用餐或退貨，故用 pose as（假扮成）；call for 是「需要」，attend to 是「照料」，engage in 是「從事」，皆不合。
空格後是 they are assigned，stores 是被派往（assigned to）的對象，子句句尾沒有 to，介系詞須移到關係代名詞前，故用 to which。
遵循標準程序、使用檢核表是為了確保一致性，避免個人的偏見（personal bias）；其餘選項與評鑑程序無關。
後面接「無緣無故與銷售員爭吵」，可知是假扮成「難纏的」（difficult）顧客；其餘形容詞與爭吵的描述不符。
蒐集資料是為了找出可「改善」（improvement）之處，並進而提升產品與服務品質；areas for improvement 為常見搭配。

zh: 神秘客是領取酬勞、受雇到商店購物並蒐集資料的消費者。他們被派往各式各樣以服務為主的企業，包括商店、餐廳和銀行——幾乎任何服務顧客的地方。神秘客有時也稱為秘密客，他們假扮成一般顧客去購買商品、在餐廳用餐、詢問事情或退貨。他們會針對被派往的商店，就產品品質、顧客服務與環境評分並提出報告。
在評鑑一家企業時，神秘客必須遵循某些標準程序，以避免個人偏見。他們通常會拿到一份檢核表，列出要觀察或留意的事項，以確保一致性。這些客人有時會蒐集關於他們「正常」觀察的資料，例如店內的整潔或服務的及時性。他們也可能假扮成難纏的顧客，無緣無故與銷售員爭論。憑藉所蒐集的資料，神秘客能找出可改善之處，進而協助提升產品與服務的品質。如此一來，這些秘密客可能幫助企業取得競爭優勢。
title: 神秘客

text: The modern worker rolls out of bed, groans, and turns off an alarm clock before reluctantly getting up for the day’s work. But how did people get to work on time before alarm clocks were widely used? During the second Industrial Age, people toiled at unusual hours in mines or factories and often had to get up for work early in the morning. They {{16}} alarm clocks because adjustable alarms had been invented by the mid-19th century. But the new device was still relatively expensive and unreliable. British workers thus relied on a human alarm clock known as a “knocker-up.” {{17}} sticks or pea shooters, the human alarms would tour the streets, tap on windows, or blast them with dried peas, trying to wake paying customers in time for work.

Whether they wielded rods or pea shooters, knockers-up became {{18}} throughout the United Kingdom. Every morning, these people, often older in age, were seen in big streets and small alleys, waking up their customers professionally. They usually would not leave people’s houses until they were sure their customers were awake.

While the practice continued in some parts of the country until the 1970s, it {{19}} as alarm clocks became more widespread and affordable. Today, beeping alarm clocks and smartphones that play morning music are surely simpler and more convenient. However, they cannot {{20}} the personal attention coming from the distinctive tap of a pea shooter.

qs.ex: could have used 表「當時本可以使用（卻沒用）」，與後句「發明已久但昂貴又不可靠」呼應；must be using 是對現在的推測，不合過去情境。
空格後接 sticks or pea shooters，分詞構句表「配備著（棍棒或豌豆槍）」，故用 Equipped with。
叫醒人遍布英國、每天清晨出現在大街小巷，所以成為人們「熟悉的身影」（familiar presences）。
此習俗隨鬧鐘普及且便宜而「衰退」（declined），與 While 引導的讓步（延續到 1970 年代）形成對比。
鬧鐘雖方便，卻「比不上」（cannot match）敲窗聲帶來的個人化關注；match 作及物動詞表「與…匹敵」。

zh: 現代上班族滾下床、哀嘆一聲，關掉鬧鐘，然後不情願地起床，準備展開一天的工作。但在鬧鐘尚未普及之前，人們是怎麼準時上班的呢？在第二次工業革命時期，人們在礦坑或工廠裡於不尋常的時段辛勞工作，往往必須在清晨起床上班。他們本來可以使用鬧鐘，因為可調式鬧鈴在十九世紀中葉就已發明。但這種新裝置仍然相對昂貴又不可靠。因此英國工人轉而仰賴一種稱為「叫醒人」（knocker-up）的人工鬧鐘。這些人工鬧鐘配備著棍棒或豌豆槍，會沿街巡行、敲打窗戶，或用乾豌豆射向窗戶，設法在付費顧客該上班的時間前把他們叫醒。
不論他們揮舞的是長桿或是豌豆槍，叫醒人在整個英國都成為人們熟悉的身影。每天早晨，這些通常年紀較長的人出現在大街小巷，專業地叫醒他們的顧客。他們通常要確定顧客確實醒來才會離開人家門前。
雖然這種做法在英國某些地方一直延續到 1970 年代，但隨著鬧鐘越來越普及、價格也越來越親民，它逐漸衰退。如今，嗶嗶作響的鬧鐘和播放晨間音樂的智慧型手機，無疑更簡單也更方便。然而，它們比不上豌豆槍獨特的敲擊聲所帶來的那份個人關注。
title: 人工鬧鐘叫醒人

text: On a hilltop overlooking the 2011-tsunami hit Otsuchi Town in northeastern Japan, there is a white phone booth standing all alone in the wind. The lonely “wind phone” serves to connect family members to their {{21}} loved ones who died in the tsunami that claimed 18,000 lives. People come to speak to those they have lost, to say the words they never got to say on that {{22}} day.

The idea for the wind phone was first {{23}} by a Japanese garden designer named Itaru Sasaki, who was grieving over the death of his cousin in 2010, before the tsunami. Feeling that he needed a private space to help him navigate through the {{24}}, Sasaki positioned a booth where he could “speak” to the dead relative. The booth he built {{25}} only an old dial phone with a disconnected phone line. When he stepped into the booth, he could pick up the phone to call his cousin, telling him how he was, and how he missed him. Sasaki stated in an interview: “Because my thoughts couldn’t be {{26}} through a regular phone line, I wanted them to be carried on the wind.” Hence, the wind phone allows Sasaki to create a one-way conversation with deep, soulful personal meaning, and renders the grieving process more {{27}} for him.

Sasaki opened his wind phone to the public in 2011, after the devastating tsunami. News about the phone gradually spread, and the booth has become a {{28}} between the living and the dead. Phones resembling the wind phone have since been built around the world. Some were even set up to allow people to call their loved ones lost in the COVID-19 pandemic.

Grieving is a natural {{29}} for coping with loss of a loved one, and people grieve in various ways. For those who speak into the wind phone, {{30}} is always there: They believe that their messages will—through some unknown way—reach the deceased.

qs.ex: 空格修飾 loved ones，需形容詞；「過世的」親人用 departed，與 who died in the tsunami 呼應。
修飾 day，需形容詞；海嘯那一天是「命運攸關的、致命的」日子，用 fateful。
被動語態 was first ___ by Sasaki，需過去分詞；idea 被「提出、產生」用 brought forth（片語動詞的過去分詞）。
the 後需名詞；為了走過喪親的「悲傷」（sorrow），他需要私人空間。
The booth he built ___ only an old dial phone：需動詞過去式，「容納／裝有」用 housed。
被動 couldn’t be ___ through a phone line：想法無法被「傳遞」，用 passed on（過去分詞）。
more ___ 為比較級形容詞，使悲傷過程變得較「可承受的」（manageable）。
a ___ between the living and the dead：名詞，「橋梁」bridge，連結生者與死者。
a natural ___ for coping：名詞，「機制」mechanism，指自然的因應機制。
主詞需名詞且接單數動詞 is：對使用者而言「希望」（hope）一直都在，冒號後說明他們相信訊息會傳達。

zh: 在日本東北部、俯瞰遭 2011 年海嘯襲擊的大槌町的一座山頂上，有一間白色電話亭孤零零地矗立在風中。這座孤單的「風之電話」讓家屬得以和在海嘯中罹難的親人連繫，那場海嘯奪走了一萬八千條人命。人們前來向失去的親人說話，說出他們在那個命運攸關的日子裡來不及說的話。

風之電話的構想最初是由一位名叫佐佐木格的日本庭園設計師提出的，他在海嘯發生前的 2010 年，正為表兄弟的過世而悲痛。他覺得自己需要一個私人空間來幫助自己走過悲傷，於是設置了一間電話亭，讓他可以和已故的親人「說話」。他所建的電話亭裡只放了一支舊式撥盤電話，電話線並未接通。他走進電話亭時，可以拿起話筒打給表兄弟，告訴他自己過得如何，以及多麼想念他。佐佐木在一次訪談中說：「因為我的思念無法透過一般電話線傳遞，所以我希望風能把它們捎過去。」因此，風之電話讓佐佐木能進行一場具有深刻心靈意義的單向對話，也使他的哀悼過程變得較能承受。
佐佐木在 2011 年毀滅性的海嘯之後，把他的風之電話對外開放。這支電話的消息逐漸傳開，這座電話亭也成為生者與死者之間的橋梁。此後世界各地陸續建造了類似風之電話的電話亭，有些甚至是為了讓人們能打給在新冠肺炎疫情中失去的親人而設置的。
哀悼是因應失去親人時一種自然的機制，而且人們哀悼的方式各不相同。對那些對著風之電話說話的人而言，希望始終都在：他們相信自己的話語會以某種未知的方式傳達給逝者。
title: 風之電話

text: In 1995, a group of business and academic leaders met at the home of Juanita Brown and David Isaacs in Mill Valley, California. None of them had any idea they were about to create a social innovation that {{11}} rapidly around the world.

The group was supposed to have a large-circle discussion in their beautiful garden. Unfortunately, it started pouring. With their plan {{12}} by the rain, the two dozen participants squeezed into the living room. They broke into small, intimate table conversations, recording their insights on paper tablecloths. They periodically stopped their conversations to switch tables so the insights and ideas might {{13}} and deepen. As they moved from one table to another, they noticed new ideas emerging from the discussions. This in turn enriched subsequent rounds of conversation. Over the course of the morning, the innovative discussion process {{14}} a new form of collective effort that transformed the depth, scope, and quality of their discussion.

The World Café was {{15}} created. Since that rainy morning in Mill Valley, the World Café approach has been applied to multi-group discussions and cooperative actions by businesses, industries, and educational institutions around the world.

qs.ex: 從過去某時間點（1995）看「即將創造、之後將迅速傳遍」的未來，用 would spread（過去未來式）。
下雨使原定計畫「被打亂」，with their plan disrupted by the rain；disrupt 與 Unfortunately 呼應。
換桌是為了讓見解與想法「流通」並深化，circulate 符合；與 deepen 並列，助動詞 might 後接原形。
討論過程「引發」（gave rise to）一種新的集體合作形式；gave rise to 表產生。
前文描述討論過程自然成形，世界咖啡館「因而」（thus）誕生，thus 表結果。

zh: 1995 年，一群商界與學術界的領袖在加州米爾谷的朱安妮塔·布朗與大衛·艾薩克斯家中聚會。他們當中沒有人料到，自己即將創造出一項日後迅速傳遍全世界的社會創新。

這群人原本預計在美麗的花園裡進行大圈圈的討論。不巧的是，下起了傾盆大雨。計畫被雨打亂後，二十幾位參與者擠進客廳。他們分成幾桌，各自進行小而親密的對話，把心得寫在紙桌巾上。他們定時停下對話去換桌，好讓各種見解與想法得以流通並加深。當他們從一桌走到另一桌時，注意到討論中浮現新的想法。這又進而豐富了後續幾輪的對話。整個早上下來，這種創新的討論方式催生了一種新的集體合作形式，改變了他們討論的深度、廣度與品質。
「世界咖啡館」就這樣誕生了。自從米爾谷那個下雨的早晨以來，世界各地的企業、產業與教育機構已將世界咖啡館的方式應用於多團體討論與合作行動。
title: 世界咖啡館

text: If you have ever been sick to your stomach on a rocking boat or a bumpy car ride, you know the discomfort of motion sickness. It can {{16}} suddenly, progressing from a feeling of uneasiness to a cold sweat. Soon, it can lead to dizziness, nausea, and vomiting.

Motion sickness occurs when the signals your brain receives from your eyes, ears, and body {{17}}. Your brain doesn’t know whether you are stationary or moving when these parts send conflicting information: One part of your balance-sensing system detects that your body is moving, but the other parts {{18}}. Your brain’s confused reaction makes you feel sick. You may experience the discomfort from the motion of cars, boats, or amusement park rides. You may also get sick from playing video games, or looking through a microscope.

You can take some {{19}} to help avoid the discomfort. If you are traveling, reserve seats where motion is felt the least, such as the front row of a car or forward cars of a train. Looking out into the distance from the vehicle can help {{20}}. You can also take medicine before your ride to avoid or reduce nausea and vomiting.

qs.ex: motion sickness 會「突然發作」，strike 表疾病、災難突然襲來；crash、flush、burst 搭配不合。
後文說各部位傳來相互衝突的訊息，故訊號彼此「不一致」（do not match）。
與前半 detects that your body is moving 對比，其餘部位「沒有偵測到」，用助動詞 don’t 代替 don’t detect；時態為現在簡單式。
為避免不適可採取「預防措施」（preventive measures），take measures 為常見搭配。
後面還說「也可以吃藥」，前句遠望「也有幫助」，用 as well（也）呼應 You can also。

zh: 如果你曾在搖晃的船上或顛簸的車程中感到想吐，你就知道動暈症的不適。它可能突然來襲，從不安的感覺發展成冒冷汗。很快地，還可能導致頭暈、噁心和嘔吐。
當大腦從眼睛、耳朵和身體接收到的訊號互不吻合時，就會發生動暈症。當這些部位傳來相互衝突的資訊時，你的大腦無法判斷你是靜止還是在移動：平衡感知系統的某一部分偵測到你的身體正在移動，但其他部分卻沒有。大腦這種困惑的反應讓你覺得不舒服。你可能因為汽車、船隻或遊樂設施的移動而感到不適，也可能因為玩電玩遊戲或看顯微鏡而感到不舒服。
你可以採取一些預防措施來避免不適。如果你正在旅行，可以預訂晃動感最小的座位，例如汽車的前排或火車前面的車廂。從交通工具往遠處望也有幫助。你也可以在搭乘前服藥，以避免或減輕噁心與嘔吐。
title: 動暈症

text: The Notre-Dame de Paris is one of the most famous cathedrals in Europe. Located at the heart of Paris, this medieval cathedral is {{21}} for its intricate architecture, stunning stained glass windows, and, above all, its bells.

Mounted in the two tall towers of the cathedral, Notre-Dame’s bells have been ringing for over 800 years. In fact, there is documented {{22}} to the ringing of bells even before the cathedral’s construction was completed, dating as far back as the 12th century. The 10 bells vary in size, each {{23}} a name. The largest one, named “Emmanuel,” weighs over 13 tons. It is the only one of the whole group that {{24}} the French Revolution, while the rest were melted down for weapons. The melted bells were recast in the late 19th century. But due to their poor acoustic quality, all of the bells were replaced in 2013—except for Emmanuel, which {{25}} its renowned, excellent sound. This particular bell, ringing in F sharp, is considered one of the most harmonically beautiful in Europe.

Over centuries, the bells have become a {{26}} part of life in Paris, where they are known as “the cathedral’s voice.” They have been used to mark the hours of the day, to call the {{27}} to prayer, and to signal emergency situations such as fires and invasions. They have also rung in times of {{28}} and of mourning, announcing such events as royal weddings and coronations of kings, as well as funerals of heads of state.

However, after the devastating fire that damaged the cathedral in 2019, the bells fell {{29}}. The building went through a complex and time-consuming process of {{30}}, and the famous monument was finally reopened on December 8, 2024. The sounds of Notre-Dame bells once again filled the air in Paris, and will be heard for generations to come.

qs.ex: is ___ for 為被動形容詞結構，be noted for 表「以…聞名」。
documented ___ to：名詞，a reference to 表「提及」，documented reference 為有文獻記載的提及。
each ___ a name：分詞構句，「各自帶有一個名字」用 bearing（現在分詞）。
that 後需動詞過去式，只有它「倖存」於法國大革命，其餘熔掉，故用 survived。
except for Emmanuel, which ___ its renowned sound：「保留」原有聲音，retained（過去式）。
a ___ part of life：形容詞，「熟悉的」生活的一部分，familiar。

與 mourning（哀悼）並列，相反詞為 celebration（慶祝）；in times of celebration，名詞。

zh: 巴黎聖母院是歐洲最著名的大教堂之一。這座中世紀大教堂位於巴黎的中心，以其精細的建築、令人驚嘆的彩繪玻璃窗，以及最重要的——鐘聲——而聞名。

聖母院的鐘架設在大教堂的兩座高塔中，鐘聲已響了八百多年。事實上，早在大教堂完工之前就有鐘聲的文獻記載，最早可追溯至十二世紀。這十座鐘大小不一，每座都有一個名字。最大的一座名叫「艾曼紐」，重達十三噸以上。它是整組鐘中唯一躲過法國大革命的，其餘的都被熔掉製成武器。被熔毀的鐘在十九世紀後期重鑄。但由於它們的音質不佳，所有的鐘在 2013 年都被更換——唯獨艾曼紐保留了下來，因為它保有著名的絕佳音色。這座鐘以升 F 音鳴響，被認為是歐洲音色最和諧優美的鐘之一。
數世紀以來，這些鐘已成為巴黎生活中熟悉的一部分，在當地被稱為「大教堂的聲音」。它們被用來報時、召喚信徒祈禱，以及為火災和入侵等緊急情況發出警訊。它們也在歡慶和哀悼的時刻響起，宣告王室婚禮、國王加冕，以及國家元首葬禮等事件。
然而，2019 年一場毀滅性大火損毀大教堂後，鐘聲沉寂了。這棟建築歷經複雜而耗時的修復過程，這座著名的古蹟終於在 2024 年 12 月 8 日重新開放。聖母院的鐘聲再度迴盪在巴黎的空中，而且將世世代代持續響下去。
title: 巴黎聖母院的鐘

text: From the campfire to the café, people have always gathered together to share the latest news. White rhinoceroses, {{11}}, do the same thing—only their choice of meeting place is a giant pile of poop.

A new study indicates that rhinos have a smelly way to {{12}}. Scientists studying white rhinos in South Africa have found that these animals leave messages in their poop. In particular, they leave their poop in the same place for all the other members in the group to smell—just like humans leaving messages on social media. Furthermore, different rhinos leave different chemicals in their poop, which provide important {{13}} about the age, sex, general health, and reproductive conditions of each specific rhino. This is of great significance for the peace and harmony in the group. When all members in a group know what’s going on with each other, it is {{14}} that they will fight.

The researchers have even made “fake poop” to see how different rhinos would react. They find that dominant males are particularly {{15}} the “fake poop” that carries chemicals from females ready to mate. The males sniff it for longer duration and come back to the same spot more frequently, a clear sign that they are gathering information about mating opportunities from the poop.

qs.ex: 插入語：人類聚在一起分享新聞，而白犀牛「結果發現也是這樣」，it turns out 語氣最自然；what is more 是「此外」，in other words 是「換句話說」，皆不合邏輯。
排泄物上留訊息是一種「溝通」方式，a smelly way to communicate；其餘動詞語意不合。
糞便中的化學物質提供關於年齡、性別等的「線索」（clues）；provide clues about 為常見搭配。
群體成員彼此了解，打架的可能性就「較低」（less likely）；it is less likely that 為句型。
優勢雄性對含有發情雌性化學物質的假糞便特別「有反應」（responsive to），後文嗅聞更久、頻繁回訪可證。

zh: 從營火到咖啡館，人們向來聚在一起分享最新消息。結果發現，白犀牛也做同樣的事——只不過牠們選擇的聚會地點是一大堆糞便。

一項新研究指出，犀牛有一種氣味強烈的溝通方式。研究南非白犀牛的科學家發現，這些動物會在糞便裡留下訊息。具體來說，牠們把糞便留在同一個地方，供群體中所有其他成員聞嗅——就像人類在社群媒體上留言一樣。此外，不同的犀牛會在糞便中留下不同的化學物質，這些物質提供了關於每隻犀牛的年齡、性別、整體健康與生殖狀況的重要線索。這對群體的和平與和諧意義重大。當群體中所有成員都知道彼此的狀況時，牠們打架的可能性就比較低。
研究人員甚至製作了「假糞便」，來觀察不同犀牛會有什麼反應。他們發現，優勢雄犀牛對帶有發情雌犀牛化學物質的「假糞便」特別有反應。雄犀牛會嗅聞較長的時間，也更頻繁地回到同一個地點，這清楚顯示牠們正從糞便中蒐集關於交配機會的資訊。
title: 犀牛的糞便訊息

text: The history of dim sum stretches back to the early days of the Silk Road, an ancient network of trade routes connecting the East and the West. Those who traveled along the routes through China needed places to rest. Teahouses thus sprang up to {{16}} the weary travelers, offering them a cup of tea to help them regain energy. But the culinary art of dim sum {{17}}, for it was considered inappropriate to pair tea with food. Centuries later, the ability of tea to aid in digestion finally became known. Teahouse owners therefore began providing bite-sized snacks as an accompaniment, and the tradition of these Cantonese delicacies was born.

Dim sum is more than just an example of Chinese cuisine. It is {{18}} an enjoyable dining experience that can span hours. The small portions were designed to merely “touch the heart,” as the name literally means, and {{19}} were first enjoyed as snacks. The small size allows the customer to order a great variety of dishes, creating a banquet of different tastes and flavors. It is customary for big groups to enjoy simple dishes together as {{20}}. Ultimately, dim sum—the food—is only a small part of the dim sum experience.

qs.ex: 茶館興起是為了「容納、接待」疲憊的旅人，accommodate 符合；其餘動詞語意不合。
點心的技藝「尚未發展」（had yet to develop），因當時認為茶配食物不恰當；與 Centuries later 形成時間對比，had yet to 為 have yet to（尚未）的過去式。
點心「意在成為」一種可持續數小時的愉快用餐體驗，be meant to be 表「本意是」。
as such 表「就此而言／因此（作為這樣的小份量）」，指小份量故最初被當作點心享用。
大夥一起享用簡單的點心，是一種「歡樂的社交活動」；呼應末句點心不只是食物。

zh: 點心的歷史可追溯到絲路的早期，絲路是連結東方與西方的古老貿易路網。沿著這些路線穿越中國的旅人需要休息的地方。於是茶館紛紛興起，用來接待疲憊的旅客，供應他們一杯茶幫助恢復體力。但點心的烹飪藝術當時尚未發展出來，因為人們認為茶配食物並不恰當。數百年後，茶有助消化的功效終於為人所知。茶館老闆因此開始提供一口大小的小點心作為搭配，這些廣式美食的傳統於是誕生。
點心不只是一種中國料理。它本意是一種可以持續數小時的愉快用餐體驗。小份量的設計只是要「點一點心」，正如其名稱字面上的意思，因此最初是被當作小點來享用。份量小讓客人能點各式各樣的菜色，形成一場各種滋味與風味的盛宴。按照慣例，一大群人會一起享用簡單的點心，作為一種歡樂的社交活動。歸根究柢，點心這種食物，只是整個點心體驗的一小部分。
title: 點心

text: Are you feeling a little guilty about your daily mid-afternoon snooze? Well, you don’t need to. Taking a nap in the middle of the day is by no means {{21}}. In fact, you are giving your brain and your body some time to recharge and turn up refreshed.

Research has shown that napping is linked with brain size and {{22}}; specifically, it can boost our cognition and memory. In our early 20s, our brain starts shrinking, which gradually slows cognition and increases dementia {{23}} in later life. The brain size of habitual nappers, however, is found to be better preserved. This suggests that napping may significantly {{24}} age-related brain shrinkage, and thus lower the possibility of developing dementia. Neurologists also confirm that naps can enhance memory and learning. For students cramming for college exams, napping will help {{25}} acquired knowledge and learned skills.

Understanding how to perfect your nap is vital for reaping its benefits. To begin with, you need to find out the ideal length of a nap. Some studies recommend napping for 20 to 40 minutes, while others {{26}} shorter naps, such as 15 to 20 minutes. The best nap length, however, may {{27}} a person’s physical condition and fatigue level. For some people, even a five-minute nap can bring about surprisingly {{28}} benefits.

Furthermore, the environment where naps are taken also plays an important role. A dark space with little distraction is ideal for napping. So, find yourself a quiet place with {{29}} light or with blackout curtains. If you can’t find a dark room, consider wearing a sleep mask. You can also add some soothing nature sounds to create a relaxing {{30}}, which can make your naps more effective.

qs.ex: by no means ___：形容詞，午睡絕非「沒有生產力的」（unproductive）；後句 In fact 說明是在充電。
linked with brain size and ___：名詞並列，「功能」（function），後句談認知與記憶功能。
increases dementia ___：名詞，增加失智的「風險」（risk）。
may significantly ___ shrinkage：原形動詞，「延緩」（delay）腦萎縮，並降低失智可能。
help ___ acquired knowledge：help 後接原形動詞，「保留」（retain）所學知識與技能。
while others ___ shorter naps：複數主詞 others 接原形動詞，「主張」用 point to，與 recommend 對比。
may ___ a person’s physical condition：助動詞後接原形，「取決於」（depend on）。
surprisingly ___ benefits：形容詞，「顯著的」（dramatic）益處，即使五分鐘小睡亦然。
with ___ light：形容詞，「極少的」（minimal）光線，與 dark space 呼應。
a relaxing ___：名詞，營造放鬆的「氛圍」（atmosphere）。

zh: 你是否對每天午後的小睡感到有點罪惡感？其實你不必如此。在白天打個盹絕非毫無生產力。事實上，你是在給大腦和身體一些時間充電，醒來後就能神清氣爽。
研究顯示，午睡與腦容量及功能有關；具體而言，它可以提升我們的認知與記憶。在二十出頭時，我們的大腦開始萎縮，這會使認知功能逐漸變得遲緩，並增加晚年罹患失智症的風險。然而，研究發現，習慣午睡者的腦容量保存得較好。這顯示午睡可能顯著延緩與年齡相關的腦萎縮，因而降低罹患失智症的可能性。神經學家也證實，午睡能增強記憶與學習。對於為大學入學考試而臨時抱佛腳的學生，午睡有助於保留所獲得的知識與學到的技能。
了解如何讓午睡更完美，對於獲得其益處至關重要。首先，你需要找出理想的午睡時間長度。有些研究建議睡 20 到 40 分鐘，而另一些則主張較短的小睡，例如 15 到 20 分鐘。然而，最佳的午睡長度可能取決於一個人的身體狀況與疲勞程度。對某些人而言，即使五分鐘的小睡也能帶來出乎意料的顯著益處。
此外，午睡所處的環境也扮演重要角色。昏暗且干擾少的空間最適合午睡。所以，替自己找一個光線極少或有遮光窗簾的安靜地方。如果找不到暗的房間，可以考慮戴眼罩。你也可以加入一些舒緩的自然音效，營造放鬆的氛圍，讓你的午睡更有效。
title: 午睡的好處
